> on_streamed function of MusicProvider - only called, when next/ previous used in UI (apparently?).

We're looking into this one, seems to be a bug. Expect to be solved soon.

> on_streamed function of MusicProvider - not called on pause

No and that is by design. It will be called when playback completed (full item played or playback stopped) which is enough imo.

> on_streamed function of MusicProvider - not called regularly

No and that is by design. Why would we want to report it regularly ?

> Which function is called, when "mark as (un)played" is used in the UI?

None, which should be fixed. I will adjust it so it calls on_streamed with 0 seconds or something (I'll chew on it a bit)

> Am I correct, that mass only supports single file based audiobooks? 

This is still topic of discussion as there seem to be multiple different implementations in the wild but the most common one is a single file per audiobook or podcast-episode with optional chapters. 
What we have now is chapter support in a single audiobook/episode. So if you have a file per chapter that will be a challenge

Could you use 

```
    async def _parse_playlist_line(self, line: str, playlist_path: str) -> Track | None:
        """Try to parse a track from a playlist line."""
        try:
            # if a relative path was given in an upper level from the playlist,
            # try to resolve it
            for parentpart in ("../", "..\\"):
                while line.startswith(parentpart):
                    if len(playlist_path) < 3:
                        break  # guard
                    playlist_path = os.path.dirname(playlist_path)
                    line = line[3:]
```

author: marcelveldt
body:
> Is there any way in my code how the queue.current_item can be none if I start playing an item?

That is a chicken and the egg situation. You get a call to play_media which initiates the playback and then you report what is playing on the "current_media" so the queue knows that as well and then sets the "current item".
So its the other way around: YOU (as player provider) need to provide the info what is active, not the other way around.

A common way to detect what is playing, is by looking at the uri/url that is loaded in the player.

Here is a possible solution? Help from ChatGPT and Copilot with the regex parts!

```
import re

def split_artists(
    org_artists: str | tuple[str, ...], allow_ampersand: bool = False
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Parse all artists from a string."""
    final_artists: list[str] = []

    splitters = [
        "featuring",
        "feat.",
        "feat",
        "duet with",
        "with",
        "ft.",
        "vs.",
        ",",
        "+",
        "/",  # handled carefully in regex
    ]
    if allow_ampersand:
        splitters.append("&")

    # Build regex pattern:
    # - For /, +, &, require spaces around to avoid splitting in names like AC/DC
    # - For others, allow optional spaces
    special_case_splitters = {"/", "+", "&"}
    pattern = r"|".join(
        rf"\s+{re.escape(s)}\s+" if s in special_case_splitters else rf"\s*{re.escape(s)}\s*"
        for s in splitters
    )
    splitter_re = re.compile(pattern, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

    artists = split_items(org_artists, allow_unsafe_splitters=False)
    for item in artists:
        subitems = splitter_re.split(item)
        for subitem in subitems:
            clean_item = subitem.strip()
            if clean_item and clean_item not in final_artists:
                final_artists.append(clean_item)

    if not final_artists:
        return artists
    return tuple(final_artists)
```

        if query_parts:

        # Main query joins the subquery

        sql_query += f" GROUP BY {self.db_table}.item_id"
        if order_by and (sort_key := SORT_KEYS.get(order_by)):

I think you have a fair point with splitting up data vs cache but we should aim at the intended way to run the server, which is containerized, so we have a controlled OS/base-layer with predictable OS-level dependencies/binaries and such.

Running the server within your own linux distro is not supported anyways, as you we have no way to guarantee that it will run, considering we depend on several binaries. The only way to run the server standalone is as development environment, in a python venv.

So, moving forward I think its OK to adjust the main entrypoint logic a bit to use the XDG environmental variables but it will not make much sense for the production setup as that will always be run as container, where the data and cache volumes will be mounted.

Your PR can then be simplified a bit with just differentiating between data and cache

author: OzGav
body:
Thanks for the suggestion! I’ve reviewed pianobar’s implementation, but there’s a key concern: pianobar uses extracted partner keys from official Pandora clients and encryption meant for specific devices. Pandora has explicitly stated that pianobar “is an unauthorized third-party application, and using it is a violation of our Terms of Use.” While they’ve tolerated it for years, it’s technically unauthorized.
This provider uses Pandora’s modern REST API (the same endpoints their website uses) with standard username/password authentication—no extracted keys or reverse-engineered encryption. The tradeoff is we can’t implement search/station creation yet, so users need to manage stations via Pandora’s official apps for now.

Just had a little play with this. Nice job!

A few things I noticed:
- Works really well playing local/smb file sources.
- Also works in the dev addon via HA ingress!

Now, it also seems to index media from **streaming** providers. When opening the 'Artist' folder, it seems to call `get_streamdetails()` for every track in there, causes a long delay for YTM for example, since resolving streamurls takes 1-2sec per Track. Playing any of the Tracks coming from a streaming provider results in an error.

I think the goal here is to only serve the content from the local/smb file providers? If so, can we configure the plugin to only advertise media items that are provided by local/smb?

author: OzGav

What do you think of only scanning at the track level so you would see the artist then album but inside would be empty if there were no local tracks? author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
> @MarvinSchenkel I think I have to do something. What do you think of only scanning at the track level so you would see the artist then album but inside would be empty if there were no local tracks? Otherwise I think it could be very slow if the provider had to scan every track of an artist just in case one had a local mapping?

The library functions should have a `provider` parameter that allows you to filter on provider. Something like this should work:

Add a constant on the top:
`SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS = ("filesystem", "filesystem_smb")`

Then inside `_get_children()`, this should work for artists
```
artists = []
for provider in SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS:
  artists.extend(await self.mass.music.artists.library_items(
      limit=limit, offset=offset, order_by="sort_name",  provider=provider
  ))
artist_items = [self._create_artist_container(artist) for artist in artists]
total = len(artists)
```

Of course we will also need this for albums, tracks, album_tracks...

author: OzGav
body:
Changing from Sequence to list caused many mypy errors. Claude summarised the issue:

This is why Sequence was used in the first place. The mypy error is telling us that:

list is invariant - so list[Radio] is NOT compatible with list[MediaItemType | BrowseFolder]
Sequence is covariant - so Sequence[Radio] IS compatible with Sequence[MediaItemType | BrowseFolder]

The issue is that browse() returns Sequence[MediaItemType | BrowseFolder], and:

Sequence[Radio] → Sequence[MediaItemType | BrowseFolder] ✅ (covariant, works)
list[Radio] → Sequence[MediaItemType | BrowseFolder] ❌ (invariant, fails)

author: OzGav
body: I simplified the ICY metadata handling by removing the redundant stream detection code and consolidating the duplicate metadata parsing logic into a single helper function. Instead of pre-checking if a stream is ICY-compatible with a separate socket connection, we now just try the normal HTTP request first and only fall back to raw socket handling if aiohttp fails to parse the response (which happens with old Shoutcast servers that return "ICY 200 OK" instead of "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"). The metadata parsing code that was duplicated in both the normal and fallback paths is now in one reusable function.

I think it's a bit weird that `ASYNC109` is choking on the parameter _names_. There's no mention about this [here](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/async-function-with-timeout/). @marcelveldt thoughts?

EDIT: Looking at this a bit more, this rule only _trigger_ based on parameters that are called `timeout`, so changing the parameter names to `timeout_seconds` is just a (dirty) workaround that (on the surface) satisfies the rule, but does not fix the underlying problem.

To be honest, I don't really see this as a problem, as the rule only triggers on helpers that intentionally have the timeout configurable, as they can be reused by multiple parts of the code (that might require different timeout values).

author: OzGav
body:
Tests added.

I had to add some type ignores in the tests because AudioTags.tags is typed as dict[str, str] but some fields (like artistsort, albumartistsort) actually store lists to match mutagen’s ID3 behavior.
The ID3 test doesn’t have this issue because it doesn’t test sort tags - the MP3 fixture doesn’t have TSOP/TSO2 (artistsort/albumartistsort) tags, so the type conflict never surfaces there.
I believe in practice this should work fine because:
	∙	Properties that access these list fields use split_items() which already handles both strings and lists
	∙	Direct string operations (.split(), .lower()) are only used on fields that genuinely are strings (like date, track, compilation)
The type hint is inaccurate but the runtime behavior is correct. The ignores are only needed in tests where we explicitly assert the list values.

As for the mdns, what makes you think this is a lot of work? author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
> > Just a few minor things, but overall, this already looks really good. Nice job!
> > As for the mdns, what makes you think this is a lot of work? I see you have already identified the mdns key in the manifest, so it should just be implementing `on_mdns_service_state_change` in the `provider.py` and basing your setup off of those ip addresses. Have a look at the airplay and bluesound providers, they already have these implemented.
> 
> Thanks!
> 
> So the main reason is that HEOS works with a single controller for all devices. mDNS finds all devices though, but we don't need all devices to be controllers. So instead of a simple mDNS device found -> MA player creation, we have to run through some kind of device host checking. For all found devices we need to loop through this (inspired by Home Assistant code):
> 
> * Check if device is already in the system from the existing controller (skip if found)
> * Connect to device, get system info (including players it found in the network)
> * Disconnect from device
> * System info reports version, connection method and players
> * Based on this info (wired + latest version), the library builds a map of 'preferred hosts'.
> * Pick 1 to connect to, store this in the integration information
> * Provider connects to stored device, loads players it can control (should be all)
> 
> Don't get me wrong, it's not that hard to get done, I just need to put some time into this, but it might be good to get this basic in the beta already ot start getting testing ;) The HEOS system does report when devices change on the network, so those are handled after the initial setup was done

Ah gotcha, totally fine to do this in a follow up PR then. Will be nice to get people to start playing with it and get you some feedback :-)

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
First off, a huge thanks for taking the effort to contribute a new music provider 👏 .

To answer your questions:

1. I would not fetch the entire track, feels like a waste of resources. What is it exactly that needs to be provided there? Otherwise I would just use the track identifier from `streamdetails.item_id`
2. That is correct. Have a test with different locales to see if the API does not return errors. If it does, then you can use something like `local = 'danish if ma_local='danish' else 'english'`
3. Yes, they are usually the 'secondary artists' of a track or album, e.g. 'XXX ft. YYY`. The artist should then be XXX and Featured artists YYY, but within MA you can just provider 1 list of artists: `[artists + featured_artists]`
4. Just double checking, some music providers differentiate favourites from library. For example, in Apple music and YT Music I can add albums and track to my library (making them accessible quickly via library > albums), but I can also like/favourite/heart a track, which makes them show up within my likes. Spotify does not have this concept, there you can only 'add to liked songs'. If your provider supports both, then map them to library / favourites accordingly. If they do not, then you can map them to library. Have a look at the providers I mentioned to see the difference for yourself
5. Tidal is indeed a good example, so you obtain them through `get_track` and set them on `metadata.lyrics` in `parse_track`.
6. Does not look familiar to me. Would be good to trace where this error is coming from (api call? during streaming?) so we can see the origin.

I'll do a more thorough review once the initial feedback has been addressed 🙏 .

Marking this PR as draft again so we know which ones we still have to give feedback to ;-). Feel free to mark it as 'ready for review' again once you have made some progress 👍 .

> 
> The specific cause is not related to tracks - it is related to shared playlists (shared by me or other users). Processing of those playlists is resolving to the library endpoint instead the catalog one, triggering a 404.

> It appears that `is_library_id` is incorrectly flagging these shared playlists as library playlists, when they are actually catalog ones. The playlists in question have a `pl.u-` prefix, which is currently (incorrectly?) passing as library.

> valid = re.findall(r"^(?:[a|i|l|p]{1}\.|pl\.u\-)[a-zA-Z0-9]+$", library_id)

> to

> valid = re.findall(r"^(?:[ailp]\.)[a-zA-Z0-9]+$", library_id)

No specific reason, it was an iteration from someone else on the previous check we had. I think we didn't have the use case of shared playlist when we implemented it.

author: marcelveldt
body:
I'm not sure why this is even needed. It seems an overly complex solution for a simply task.
My proposal would be that the party mode provider adds custom api commands for enqueuing items an dthat the guest mode frontend talks to those custom commands.

In the provider code of the guest mode itself, it can simply call the existing public methods of the queue controller.
So, the guest mode provider is in control over the whole process of the guest mode party mode and accepts commands from the special/limited guest mode frontend and then handles all logic to finally call the queue controller for the actual action.

This also allows for the system admin to use normal queue operations to overrule the party mode.
Like I said before, keep the logic for party mode isolated in the party mode provider which I think is perfectly doable with the right architecture. We have added the "extra_attributes" attribute to both the PlayerQueue and PlayerQueueItem models so you can store custom data in these objects to help the provider.

body:
My plan has always been to add a on-disk cache (as you could also see in the comment I left in the code) so if we want to touch this now, I want to go with a disk cache as that makes much more sense. We can also combine it with a limited FIFO cache to cache the last 50 thumbnails or something but in the end you just do not want to go through ffmpeg every time to grab the thumbnail.

When using the normal MA webinterface I am 100% confident that the images are cached by the browser but as you confirmed, this is not the case with any external tools accessing the MA data.

Let me know if you want us/me to fix the disk cache or you like to give it a stab yourself.
I think we need to create a safe hash of the path to store on disk and append a size;

So something like this 

provider + item_id ==> some hash string
thumbnails folder (subfolder of data dir)
hash_{size}.jpg
etc.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
That's exactly the info I was after. It looks like YTM internally stores this value as the album id for a track that was manually uploaded. Now of course we cannot link this to any album out there, which ultimately causes this error.

My suggestion is to **prevent this value from ever creeping into MA**. So instead of failing on a invalid album id in the `helpers.py`, we could just simply extend [this](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/fdf1ad5e6ad69dfbb8361cc753cc1e21bd3a05d0/music_assistant/providers/ytmusic/__init__.py#L928) check by checking if the album id is a valid id (e.g. `and track_obj["album"]["id"].startswith("MPRE")`). This will only add the Album to the track if the id is valid, preventing your album id from ever being synced to MA in the first place.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body: > Updated my reply post above with what I feel are very strong arguments why it would only make logical sense that this player provider for the Linkplay protocol should be named Linkplay Player Provider (and use the Linkplay logo) instead of being named just after Linkplay’s first-party product brand (which is also using Linkplay streaming protocol). The protocol is called Linkplay after the company that license it and just so also happens to use that Linkplay technology in their own WiiM branded products: > > * https://www.linkplay.com > > PS: This is also why it makes sense that the existing Home Assistant’s integration is named Linkplay (and not WiiM) when it is compatible with both first-party and third-party brands that uses the Linkplay streaming protocol, (because that integration is named after the protocol and not only after the first-party brand of product that uses it, similar to how the Google Cast integration is not named after Google Nest today). > > * https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/linkplay > > * https://www.linkplay.com/aboutus > * https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/linkplay > > LinkPlay is an OEM manufacturer with indeed their own consumer brand named WiiM. This provider is _specifically_ aimed at providing support for the WiiM supported Link Play features. So while this provider _may_ work with other LinkPlay players, we do not want to give off the impression that it will work with _all_ Linkplay players. Furthermore, Linkplay themselves have told us that they would like to be added via the _consumer_ brand which is WiiM, so the name will be WiiM provider.

body:
Just had a look at the `pywiim` package and it seems they also support enqueing. MA also has an enqueue mode (as opposed to the flow mode) that enqueues single items instead of playing 1 long stream url. The benefit is twofold:
* Rich, per song metadata
* Max audio quality. Flow mode resamples to 48khz/16bit

You can have a look at the Sonos provider to see how you could support both enqueue and flow mode in 1 provider. I would suggest to leave this for now and do it later in a follow up PR as an enhancement.

author: marcelveldt
body:
@Hedda we had a chat about this with LinkPlay itself and they stated as following;
They are a OEM manufacturer of the LinkPlay (base)chip that vendors can use to create their own audio devices.
While the base LinkPlay chip and api delivers a foundation, every vendor has unique features built on top of that.

Next to that they have their own brand targeted to consumers directly, which is WiiM (which is also the most known one in our community) - which is based on their standard LinkPlay chip but also has a lot of features on top of it.

While you can ofcourse control all base functionality with a generic LinkPlay library (or even the WiiM library), you will not be able to support all features of all devices that use the LinkPlay chip, you would need to implement a library for Vendor A, B and C.

Their own WiiM app is a good example. You can fully control all WiiM devices in there. Other LinkPlay devices do show up (and you can also group them just fine) but you won't be able to control all their features, simply because that is manufacturer specific. Next to that there is also consent. While LinkPlay gave approval (and their support) to implement a HA integration + library and provider in MA for their WiiM devices, they can not give that same consent for other vendors.

The contributor here is focused on WiiM devices and wants to make a provider that works well for the WiiM devices specifically, also most likely because he owns WiiM device(s) himself and not other LinkPlay generic ones. Which I think is perfectly fine.

You can then challenge if this WiiM provider should also support at least the base features of all other LinkPlay based devices (just like the WiiM app does) or you ALSO get a LinkPlay generic provider, a Vendor A provider, a Vendor B provider etc.

For the Home Assistant integration it will be a generic LinkPlay integration (which already exists today) and a WiiM-only integration which only supports the WiiM devices in the full featureset.

If somebody steps up and wants to create a LinkPlay generic provider, that would ofcourse be very welcome but now the PR author focuses on WiiM devices, which is very understandable and I'm sure it will make lots of people very happy as the WiiM devices are very beloved in the community.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
> @MarvinSchenkel re: [#3147 (review)](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3147#pullrequestreview-3812949920)
> 
> Addressed in commits [58e49800](https://github.com/trudenboy/ma-server/commit/58e49800) and [31ab2ea5](https://github.com/trudenboy/ma-server/commit/31ab2ea5):
> 
> * Removed the Preload streaming mode entirely — no more downloading/caching entire tracks to disk
> * Removed the Direct mode as well, leaving only Buffered (bounded async queue, decrypt on-the-fly)
> * `CONF_STREAMING_MODE` config entry removed; stream buffer size remains as an Advanced setting
> * Cleaned up ~430 lines of streaming infrastructure (temp file management, direct mode, preload logic)

As I tried to say in my previous comment, a music provider cannot do *any* form of downloading / buffering, whether that's in memory or to a file. Same for functionality like seeking. This is all handled in core functionality by MA. The only thing you should do is return an HTTP url + a decryption key (which you can set on the StreamDetails). Our core logic will then decrypt and play the url via ffmpeg. See Apple Music as an example of how you can play encrypted streams. 

This practically means you have to get rid of a lot of code you are trying to add in this PR and set the appropriate fields to let MA handle everything. Please let me know if you have any questions about this.

body:
Kinda agreeing with @chrisuthe here. I think playlists should only be able to hold **directly playable items**, such as Tracks, Podcast episodes, Audiobooks and radio streams. 

I think we should postpone support for 'Containers' such as genres, albums etc. when we introduce the 'dynamic playlist' feature we have been talking about for a while now. The (still not spec'ed) idea is that we add some sort of rule-based mechanism for dynamic playlist, e.g. "30% genre Pop + 20% Album X + 50% radio mode over playlist Y".

I feel this is the more logical place for these kind of MediaTypes as opposed to static playlists. Thoughts?

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
No the spec is the 'Sendspin spec' which can be found [here](https://www.sendspin-audio.com/spec/). It's basically tells how clients and servers should interact. MA always needs to implement a player provider according to the 'player provider specs'. If MA wants to do something on top of that, MA needs to counter for it (e.g. by sending a stop instead of a pause).

I think this still allows all your use cases because MA can definitely pause sendspin players, the only thing it will do under the hood is it will stop the stream and then start it from t=30s for example.

body: > Sorry for the delay. I was on vacation with the family last week > > Thanks for the feedback @MarvinSchenkel — great question. Dashie is different than Fully Kiosk here in that it's both a **player** (receives audio from MA) and has a **display/controller** built-in natively. It'll show music playing information as a pop-up and alongside the screensaver as well as support transferring music between speakers. > > Here's what the tablet UI looks like in practice: > > > These features are why the streams controller endpoints were added — the tablet needs to query MA for player state, player list, and recently played items. The provider itself only handles the player direction (MA → device), but the display/controller direction (device → MA) needs these endpoints. > > I agree they don't belong in the streams controller. Should I move them into the provider using `mass.streams.register_dynamic_route()` (same pattern as Sonos, Squeezelite, DLNA, etc.), or would you prefer a different approach for this kind of display/controller use case? Those are two completely different use cases. Let's scope this PR to what we intended to do with this: Add the Dashie player provider. Generally, when you want to obtain information from MA (eg player states), you would use the default MA API for this. Users can generate a long lived token and add that in Dashie, so that dashie can query the MA api for this information. We cannot register dynamic routes for this use case, since this is not the intended purpose.

author: marcelveldt
body:
MA's syncgroups are designed to work with standard players that support set_members. It is a wrapper that basically creates a virtual group around players that can normally only sync individual members and the player/provider has no concept of groups at all.

If Snapcast actually supports groups natively, why don't you implement this directly ?
Implement ProviderFeature.CREATE_PLAYER_GROUP and expose snapcast groups as PlayerType.GROUP

Basically implement your own variant of syncgroup but one that is tailored on snapcast.
I think that is better than trying to sync MA syncgroups back to snapcast and vice versa - that gets messy very fast

author: OzGav

author: marcelveldt
body:
Point is that the underlying providers should not have to deal with the syncgroups at all - you are mixing up responsibilities here. Like I stated before, a SyncGroup is a MA higher level detail. Underlying players and their providers should not interact with that directly.

A SyncGroup picks a leader dynamically - for the sake of a player/provider, all they have to deal with is a player and synced players to it. They have no knowledge of the syncgroup umbrella above it from MA and it should stay this way.

If you want to bring groups to snapcast, you'll need to implement the groups in the snapcast provider.

body:
Can we focus on one thing at a time in the PR please ?

- MediaType.RADIO needs to changes now - that is for ordinary radio streams and already works fine today. If not, open a focused PR on that alone.
- We want to add support for playlists with the "is_dynamic" set to True so lets handle that in this PR.
- Let's please try to use as much of the existing logic as possible where we already watch the end of the queue and refill dynamic tracks.
- When we add a dynamic playlist to the queue, let's automatically add that to the "radio items" of the queue, so teh user is informed that there is a dynamic component active. Users already know the "radio mode" concept so this way they dont have to learn something new.


@MarvinSchenkel implemented most of the current "radio mode" features which is working on based on similar tracks. Let's try to get this over the finish line with reusing/extending as much of our existing structure as possible. In the end the concept is the same: Our current generic radio mode dynamically fills the queue (but gets similar tracks based on the reference) and this new dynamic playlists just automatically enable radio mode and provide the dynamic tracks themselves.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
Bpm and Key are not part of `MediaItem` / `Track` level, but rather on the actual stream level (the audio). I am currently working on a new type of provider called `AudioAnalysisProvider` which will capture this information automatically by analyzing the pcm audio. 

These metrics will be stored in an [`AudioAnalysis` model](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/8b34aef84398913e901b89d01bb97e2c192d535a/music_assistant/models/audio_analysis.py#L23), but this on the `Track's provider` level, not the `Track`.

However, I think it makes sense to leverage the information when music providers provide them, so I was thinking it makes sense that we introduce a new `ProviderFeature.AUDIO_ANALYSIS` that we call during a music provider sync in order to grab those metrics and store them in the `AudioAnalysis` object without having to do any pcm audio analysis. Then we can also read those metrics from ID3 tags on local files

def my_function(param1: str, param2: int, param3: bool = False) -> str:

    :param param1: Description of what param1 is used for.

> > > **Extract `music_assistant/helpers/yandex_auth.py`** with:
> > > 
> > > * `YandexQRAuth` class (QR session + polling + token exchange)

author: marcelveldt
body:
Pushed b20f6e956 with the bigger refactor:

- supports_dynamic_leader_switching moved to PlayerProvider (as discussed, ProviderFeature comes later when we bump the models package).
- handoff_sync_leadership now takes new_leader + remaining_members and does both halves of the handoff in one call — old leader steps out, remaining members are attached to the new leader. Sync group no longer needs the follow-up cmd_set_members.
- Dropped the cached _active_protocol_domain field entirely. Replaced with a derived `active_protocol_domain` property that reads the live state: returns the leader's active protocol iff a member still requires it, otherwise falls back to the leader's native domain. Downshift is automatic, no explicit clear-on-removal needed.
- _any_member_requires_protocol_domain stays in sync_group (it iterates the member set, which is sync_group's concern). _active_protocol_supports_dynamic_leader_switching is gone — inlined as `session_player.provider.supports_dynamic_leader_switching` at the one callsite.

body:
This does not make a lot of sense to me and I'm against adding this.
AirPlay is by default completely based around mdns and we even need to read properties from mdns to offer things like encryption and pairing. In a normal domestic network setup, mdns will work fine. 

Trying to use these protocols in an environment is was never intended for (e.g. enterprise grade networks) will just give issues. 

Adding this will hurt more than it solves imo.

author: marcelveldt
body:
We state clearly in our documentation that we do not support advanced network deployments like vlans etc. and both MA and the speakers must be on the same (v)LAN. 

If you want to isolate your speakers and/or IoT devices from your main network, an easy fix is to simply put MA on that same (v)LAN or even make the host multi homed. We offer advanced settings to set the bind addresses and publish addresses for this purpose.

By far the most support issues come from people with non standard network or host setups. It's simply not fair in comparison to put this strain on mostly community volunteers providing support so I think as a project we have the right to be reluctant to supporting these kind of setups. In the end the people that really know what they're doing will figure it out anyways.

For simpler protocols like Sonos and Cast we already provide this manual IP option because those are much simpler. You just need the IP to connect to and done. AirPlay is different because the entire protocol is mdns based. If we accept this manual addresses, the next thing that will happen is issue reports that people can not pair their devices etc. Also DACP will stop working (for routing commands from player to server). Long story short: It will not work properly and it will be a support nightmare.

I'm sorry for the efforts already put in this PR but we simply can not merge everything.

author: OzGav
body:
Thanks for taking a look. Looking at it more deeply I think these are actually compatible and we don’t need to pick one as they solve different problems.

Your Artist.type is the artist’s primary identity (what they mostly are — narrator, author, singer, composer). That’s what your audiobook PR needs, and it’s a useful field to keep.

Our Credit with ArtistRole is the per-relationship role — what this artist does on this specific track. Classical music (and could be extended to all music types) needs this because the same person can play multiple roles on the same recording (Karajan is both conductor and main artist on a Beethoven track) and different roles across recordings (some performers also compose). We can’t collapse that to a single per-Artist type without losing information.

On the performance point — both approaches are DB-side queries, not Python filtering. Ours filters on track_artists.role, yours filters on artist_id. Both are indexed; neither is slower.

Concretely I’d suggest: keep your Artist.type for primary type / audiobook browse, and if mine gets up then I’ll keep Credit for per-track-relationship role. They sit at different layers and serve different queries.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Hi @iVolt1, thanks a lot for the work you put into this PR — really appreciate the thought you put into the seek-bar / signal-chain / pause-resume scenarios.

We've taken a step back and reviewed this PR alongside the related plugin-source bug reports and the broader feedback we've been getting. The conclusion we reached is that the underlying model wasn't the right fit: independent contributors kept reaching for the same workaround (faking a `PlayerQueue` so the frontend would render correctly), which is a signal the abstraction itself needed to change rather than each provider papering over it.

We've now opened #3938 which promotes plugin sources to first-class `AudioSource` MediaItems — browseable from a new "Live Inputs" node, played through the standard `play_media` / streamdetails pipeline, and rendered by the existing queue UI without any fake-queue indirection. Live metadata flows through `streamdetails.stream_metadata` (the same channel ICY radio uses), control commands proxy through a single `on_source_control` hook, and exclusivity is enforced via `ResourceBusyError` from `get_stream_details`.

The specific concerns this PR addressed are covered by the refactor:
- Seek bar / progress — solved by single-queue-item streaming with stream_metadata.elapsed_time
- Pause/resume reliability — the queue item stays active across transient pauses; the seek bar freezes naturally
- Source takeover from local content — covered by the standard play_media flow replacing the queue item
- Signal-chain display — works out of the box via the standard streamdetails path

Going to close this one in favor of #3938 — thanks again for surfacing the gaps, this refactor wouldn't have happened without the issues being raised here.

author: marcelveldt

Hi @trudenboy, thanks for the work on this — really appreciate the thought you put into the handoff state machine and the opt-in UI integration.

We've taken a step back and reviewed this PR alongside the related plugin-source bug reports and the broader feedback (incl. #3857 which reaches for the same fake-queue workaround). The conclusion we reached is that the underlying model wasn't the right fit: independent contributors keeping landing on the same workaround is a signal the abstraction itself needed to change.

#3938 promotes plugin sources to first-class `AudioSource` MediaItems — browseable from a new "Live Inputs" node, played through the standard `play_media` / streamdetails pipeline, and rendered by the existing queue UI without any fake-queue indirection. Live metadata flows through `streamdetails.stream_metadata` (the same channel ICY radio uses), control commands proxy through a single `on_source_control` hook.

The yandex_ynison provider is fully migrated in that PR. You'll want to rebase / re-port your handoff-state-machine improvements against the new contract — `get_audio_sources()` returns the `AudioSource`, `get_stream_details(source_id, queue_id)` returns the StreamDetails (raising `ResourceBusyError` on exclusive collisions), `get_audio_stream(streamdetails)` matches the MusicProvider signature, and your `_on_play/pause/next/previous/seek` methods are dispatched from `on_source_control` instead of being assigned as callbacks. Live metadata updates go through `mass.streams.update_stream_metadata(queue_id, StreamMetadata(...))`.

Happy to help with the rebase if you hit anything tricky.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Hi @trudenboy, heads-up: #3938 just landed a refactor of the plugin sources architecture. Plugin sources are now first-class `AudioSource` MediaItems and the `PluginProvider` contract has changed — your DLNA receiver provider will need a small migration to land on top of `dev`:

- `get_source()` → `async def get_audio_sources() -> list[AudioSource]`
- `get_audio_stream(player_id)` → `get_audio_stream(streamdetails, seek_position)` (same shape as `MusicProvider` — no `player_id` parameter)
- Add `async def get_stream_details(source_id, queue_id) -> StreamDetails` (raises `ResourceBusyError` on exclusive collisions)
- The `on_play`/`on_pause`/`on_next`/`on_previous`/`on_seek`/`on_volume`/`on_select` callback fields are replaced by `async def on_source_control(source_id, action, value)` and the optional `async def on_source_selected(source_id, player_id, queue_id)` hook
- Live metadata updates go through `mass.streams.update_stream_metadata(queue_id, StreamMetadata(...))` (same channel radio ICY uses)

Canonical migration example: [`vban_receiver`](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/feat/audio-sources/music_assistant/providers/vban_receiver/provider.py); the demo template at `_demo_plugin_provider` shows the recommended shape for new providers.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Hi @Odn0, heads-up: #3938 just landed a refactor of the plugin sources architecture. The old `PluginProvider.get_source()` only allowed one source per provider instance — that limit is gone in the new model, so a SoundTouch Favorites provider can now naturally return one `AudioSource` per favorite.

The new contract on the provider:

- `async def get_audio_sources() -> list[AudioSource]` — return one AudioSource per favorite
- `async def get_stream_details(source_id, queue_id) -> StreamDetails` per session (raises `ResourceBusyError` on exclusive collisions if applicable)
- `async def get_audio_stream(streamdetails, seek_position)` for CUSTOM streams (matches the `MusicProvider` signature)
- `async def on_source_control(source_id, action, value)` for proxying play/pause/next/prev/seek/volume to the device
- Optional `async def on_source_selected(source_id, player_id, queue_id)` hook for reacting to selection

AudioSources are browseable under the new top-level "Live Inputs" node, are favoritable, and play through the standard `play_media` flow. Canonical example: [`vban_receiver`](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/feat/audio-sources/music_assistant/providers/vban_receiver/provider.py); the demo template at `_demo_plugin_provider` shows the recommended shape.

- `get_audio_stream(player_id)` → `get_audio_stream(streamdetails, seek_position)` (matches `MusicProvider`)

Canonical example: [`vban_receiver`](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/feat/audio-sources/music_assistant/providers/vban_receiver/provider.py); also see the sibling `yandex_ynison` migration in the refactor PR.

author: OzGav
body:
The problem this solves is cosmetic. Audio plays fine over plain HTTP, the only thing that doesn't work is the album art showing in the Sonos app. If you controlled your music through Music Assistant you would never see a problem. So this only affects people who use the native Sonos app with MA as a background source, and even then it's just a missing thumbnail.

To fix that, the change asks the user to run a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front of the stream server, and then it swaps the address MA gives to every player, not just Sonos. That's a potential problem. A lot of local players like Squeezebox and older DLNA speakers can't do HTTPS, so anyone who turns this on to fix the Sonos art could end up breaking audio on their other speakers without realising why. 

My question is whether this is worth a permanent setting in core. It's a narrow case, it's cosmetic, and MA on its own isn't affected. One alternative is to document a reverse proxy setup for the people who really want it. If we do decide it's worth having, I suggest it should be limited to the Sonos player so it can't affect everyone's other speakers.

`mass.music.search` has a stable, known signature — `search_query`, `media_types`, `limit`, `library_only` — and returns a typed `SearchResults `object. The entire `_search_media_items` function with its multiple kwargs/positional arg attempts, and `_iter_search_result_items` with its attribute probing, should be replaced with a single direct call. Similarly` _media_item_title` and `_media_item_value` should use the typed attributes on the SearchResults member models rather than getattr chains.

SearchResults has typed attributes,  `artists`, `albums`, `genres`, `tracks`, `playlists`, `radio`, `audiobooks`, `podcasts `. So `_media_item_title, _media_item_value`, and `_iter_search_result_items` should all be rewritten against the actual typed models (Artist, Album, Track, Radio etc.) which all have a name attribute and uri from their base class. Additionally, `MEDIA_TYPE_OPTIONS` includes types like FOLDER, ANNOUNCEMENT, FLOW_STREAM that have no corresponding field on SearchResults and can never return search results so these should either be removed or handled explicitly

author: marcelveldt
body:
This PR goes a bit against our whole recommendation that players should be on the same vLAN (or flat network) as players and the streams server provides a simple, painless way to stream the audio to players. There is a reason that the streamserver does not add HTTPS by default as it adds unneeded overhead and a lot of players even struggle with HTTPS, especially the older ones.

Maybe this works for Sonos players but it will fail for others.

The whole idea of this streams server being detached from the normal webserver is that we can provide the players on the network this direct connection, without the overhead.

Putting the streams server behind a reverse proxy is just a bad idea. 
You may be knowing what you are doing but also a lot of people don't and then end up filing support requests that stuff is not working properly. It may even set the wrong expectation that the streams server can be exposed on the internet. It is NOT, its meant to be served only locally on your network. Imagine what will happen if somebody (accidentally) opens it up on the internet.

So I'm inclined to say that this PR should not be accepted in this form.
In normal situations your players should just be on the same L2 network as the MA server and there is no reason to not do that unless complicating your setup. So maybe start with your reasoning why you want it setup this way.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
**`_detect_image_format` mis-detects versioned local covers as JPEG**

The `?cs=<checksum>` suffix added by `_versioned_image_path` defeats extension-based format detection. `_detect_image_format` (`music_assistant/controllers/metadata.py`) does:

```python
match pathlib.PurePath(path).suffix.lower():
    case ".svg": ...
    case ".png": ...
    case _: return "jpg"
```

For a versioned local cover path like `cover.png?cs=abc123`, `PurePath(...).suffix` is `.png?cs=abc123`, which matches no case and falls through to the `jpg` default. The result is that PNG/GIF folder covers (`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = {"jpg","jpeg","png","gif"}`) are now re-encoded/served as JPEG, losing transparency — a regression vs. the previous clean `cover.png` path.

The embedded-cover case is unaffected (its path points at the audio file, which already defaulted to jpg).

Suggested fix — strip the query before suffix detection:

```python
match pathlib.PurePath(path.split("?", 1)[0]).suffix.lower():
```

author: OzGav
body: Agreed. The `?cs=` suffix makes `PurePath("cover.png?cs=abc").suffix` return `.png?cs=abc`, which falls through to the jpg default and re-encodes PNG/GIF covers. Fixed by stripping the query before suffix detection which is safe to do because a real filesystem path never contains ?, so normal paths are unaffected

author: OzGav
body:
I think this is actually a bug, separate from AcoustID. We already track staleness as the coverage endpoint reports `stale_version`, and `start_analysis` re-runs analysis when a stored row is below the provider’s current version. But the nightly scan never acts on it, its candidate query picks tracks purely on whether a row exists, NOT on version. 

So once any row exists, the scan skips that track forever, and stale rows only ever get refreshed when a track happens to be played. After a provider bumps its `analysis_version`, the background scan won’t re-analyse anything — a track you never play keeps its outdated analysis indefinitely.

So the controller change makes the scan’s candidate query version-aware: a track is offered when it has no row, OR its row is below the provider’s current version. That fixes the stale-rescan gap for every provider, and the AcoustID -1 retry just builds on the corrected behaviour.

author: OzGav
body:
I tested this locally (mock stream server + the live flow endpoint + VLC) to pin down the mechanism. Whilst I could see the double open (VLC opens a probe connection without `Icy-MetaData`, sees the `icy-*` headers, drops it and reconnects with `Icy-MetaData: 1`), it's purely a VLC/LibVLC behaviour — it only happens when `icy-*` headers are present (toggle them off and VLC opens a single connection; curl/wget always open one).

BUT... MA handles the duplicate connections cleanly. Reproducing the probe → drop → reconnect against the live flow endpoint (with a Cast player streaming at the time) didn't disturb anything: two concurrent GETs to the same flow URL both return byte-identical audio, the dropped probe just logs Ignored premature client disconnection, and the active playback was unaffected. VLC also fully decodes the stream with the icy-* headers present (FLAC included). So the PR premise — that the second open "splits/aborts the session and playback dies" — doesn't seem to hold; the worst it costs is a throwaway probe connection and a duplicate ffmpeg chain.

Having said that, the first part of this PR (only sending the ICY headers when ICY metadata is actually requested) seems harmless in the broader context and it's a slight improvement, since right now a player with ICY disabled still gets `icy-name/description/version/logo` because they're merged unconditionally. So I think that part would be ok to merge.

The second part (removing `icy-name` from `DEFAULT_STREAM_HEADERS`) seems unnecessary and I think might have impact beyond the flow stream because I believe it would also strip `icy-name` from the announcement stream and the universal-group flow stream, neither of which are part of the AmpliPi path. Could that part be dropped, or scoped to the flow stream / the existing per-player ICY-disabled setting, to keep the blast radius minimal?

Why do we need custom menu's etc. ?
We can simply do this as a metadata provider. Have some settings with preferences.
Change the background scan logic a tiny bit of the metadata controller maybe
And all set. Less complicated, way more flexible.

Want to refresh the metadata ? We have the existing "update metadata" and "refresh item" calls

author: marcelveldt
body:
Thanks for digging into this @OzGav, and for getting the OP to test! After tracing it I think this is a symptom of a cause one level up, so I went with a root-cause fix instead.

For a sync group whose leader is a Universal Player outputting via AirPlay (shairport-sync), the group never resolves its current item because `UniversalPlayer.current_media` returns `None` while outputting through a protocol player. The sync group mirrors that raw value, so `_update_queue_from_player` bails out early and never reaches the live-metadata refresh — which is why it updated once at startup and then froze.

#4303 fixes that at the player level: the universal player now surfaces the active output protocol player's `current_media`, so the existing per-second update path refreshes live metadata for grouped AirPlay exactly like every other player — no extra background task. As a bonus it also unfreezes the current item/progress for those groups, not just the radio title.

Going to close this in favour of #4303, but thanks a lot — your clear repro and the logs made this much easier to pin down. 🙏

Looking back at my notes and the logs when I reproduced the problem. At a real track end the group reported BUFFERING with currentTime ≈ the streamed length, and never IDLE/FINISHED so from that I assumed EOF was ignored. And then the group only ever went IDLE after MA sent the new LOAD, with idleReason: 'INTERRUPTED'. 

Whilst the issue is only with Cast devices I assumed that it could happen with others hence the fix in the player queues controller. 

On doing the fix in the cast provider instead I think we would basically spot that we're in flow mode and the player's sat buffering at the end, and mark it as stopped so the normal next-track logic takes over. The one catch is telling a real end from a normal mid-song network buffer. To do that safely the provider needs to know how much we'd actually streamed, and that lives on the queue/streams side at the moment. So we'd either pass that down to the provider, or fall back to something like "it's been buffering too long" which is a bit less safe.

author: OzGav
body:
I tried this and moved the detection into the cast provider where I mapped flow-mode BUFFERING-after-PLAYING to IDLE once `current_time` is past a threshold and with the changes to the queue-controller reverted.

It works fine for normal-length tracks, but it stalls on short ones. First repro track was a 14s intro (2Cellos – Thunderstruck  (Intro)) and at the rate change the group reported:

 `playerState: 'BUFFERING', currentTime: 14.258367`

 …and then just sat there (still BUFFERING through the next GET_STATUS poll, never recovered). With a 30s gate it never fires.

The problem is that `current_time` is the streamed length of the flow session at the restart, not the track length so it resets on each restart. So the problem is "short leading track in a session, then a higher-rate track forces the restart." We could accept a stall on those and lower the threshold, but it doesn't fully close it and 15s wouldn't my test case (14.26s); I'd have to drop to ~10s, which starts overlapping possible mid-song network rebuffering and risks false end-of-stream detection.

The reason the controller version doesn't need a magic number is that it compares the player's reported position against what we actually streamed (total_streamed), so it resumes correctly at ~14s.

So I see three ways to go:
1. Provider-side, fixed threshold. Simplest and keeps it out of the controller, but accepts a stall on short leading tracks 
(manual skip to recover), and no single threshold is safe (too high stalls short tracks, too low false-triggers on network  buffering).
2. Provider-side, fed the real signal. Pass total_streamed (or just a "flow stream finished sending" flag) down to the cast 
provider so its buffering→idle decision is robust. Keeps the state correction in the provider like you suggested, at the cost of the provider depending on queue/streams state.
3. Controller-side (current PR) . No magic number and no stall, because the "has it finished?" check already sits next to the total_streamed / queue_buffer_completed state it needs.

Thoughts?

author: marcelveldt
body:
The streams server should simply not/never be behind a reverse proxy. It is meant to serve audio to locally connected clients only. The Sonos player itself should also get an URL to the artwork from the stream server.

We will not/never support hosting the streams server behind any reverse proxy for reasons I mentioned above.
There simply is no reason to do so. What you can do is make sure that your Sonos speakers an directly access the MA host at all times. Consider a multi-homed network setup for instance.

The streams server is a (deliberately) simple, unauthenticated http only webserver to serve audio to the various players MA supports. The webserver however (on a dedicated TCP port) is fully protected, authenticated and can be hosted on HTTPS, reverse proxy etc.

I'm going to close this PR for these reasons but thanks anyways for filing it.

author: marcelveldt
body:
thanks for the detailed investigation here @jyundt, the root cause analysis in the linked issue is spot on 👍

I'm a bit hesitant about the `volume_map` approach though, it feels like it's doing more work than needed and I'd rather not introduce a learned calibration table for this.

The thing is: for RAOP we always have to start cliraop with a `-volume`, so we can't just skip sending one. But the value we want isn't the parent's native volume - that's a different scale, which is exactly what causes the drift. It's the volume the device itself reports back to us over DACP (`dmcp.device-volume=`). That one is already on the airplay scale, so re-sending it on a stream restart is basically a no-op and the receiver stays put. In other words the device already tells us the right number, so we don't need to calculate/translate it.

So I think this can be reduced to:

- keep the DACP volume feedback enabled for players with a native parent, so the child keeps mirroring the device's own volume into `stored_volume` like it already does today
- in `sync_volume_level`, for a native parent, don't overwrite the child with the parent volume but just keep the child's own (stored) value

That drops the need for `CONF_VOLUME_MAP`, the seeding logic and the linear translation entirely.

The only thing we can't fully avoid is a cold start (or a volume change while nothing is streaming), since RAOP doesn't let us read the device volume before opening a session - so the first stream nudges the volume once and then the feedback corrects + stores it. That's a one-time, self-correcting nudge instead of drifting on every track change.

I'll set this to draft for now, let me know what you think and happy to help if anything's unclear!

author: marcelveldt
body:
Hi @Odn0 — first, thank you for the work here and for patiently working through all the review rounds. 🙏

I really wanted to get this one over the finish line, so rather than leave it in limbo I reshaped it into the form we can accept and merge: a native **Bose SoundTouch player provider**. To be clear — this stays **your** contribution: you're kept as code owner, your commits are preserved, and the preset-button feature you built is fully intact. I've pushed the changes on top of your branch.

What changed and why:
- The speakers are now **detected on the network** (mDNS + manual IP) and owned by Music Assistant as native Bose SoundTouch players, instead of layering on top of whatever provider happened to discover them.
- They expose native control over the local SoundTouch API: **power, volume, mute, transport, source selection and multiroom (zone) grouping**.
- `PLAY_MEDIA` is deliberately **omitted** — SoundTouch has no usable API to play an arbitrary stream — so actual audio is delegated to a **linked playback protocol (DLNA)** through our protocol-linking mechanism (the provider `depends_on` dlna). That's why the speakers "just play" without us reinventing streaming.
- Your **preset buttons** live on as a per-player setting: each speaker's settings has the same search-and-assign flow you built, and a physical press plays the configured item.
- **Announcements** are supported natively when you set a Bose developer app key in the provider settings: they're sent as an overlay that ducks the current music and resumes it afterwards (like Sonos). Without a key, announcements simply fall back through the linked protocol. (A shared MA-wide key isn't viable — the free tier is rate-limited per key — so it's opt-in per install.)

Because I don't have SoundTouch hardware here, the parts that need your eyes on real devices are: DLNA-linked playback, the multiroom zone grouping, source selection, now-playing metadata, native announcements, and the preset-press detection (I kept your tested detection logic). You know these devices far better than I do — please give it a spin and tweak anything that needs it.

Thanks again for sticking with it! 🙌

author: marcelveldt
body:
Can we hold off with this one until @chrisuthe is done with refactoring recommendations ?
In short the idea is that we're going to separate recommendations from their items.
So any provider can inform what recommendations are supported (quick call, no lookups at all, just static list).

Per recommendation(row) the provider also sets a flag if this recommendation may be enabled by default (which we should use very carefully and only do on the very common ones).

Then the client (frontend, mobile app or any other MA client) can decide what rows to actually show, based on the user preferences setting of enabled rows. More rows can be discovered by editing the discovery page (which we should maybe make a bit more clear).

This not only brings a massive performance boost versus now (because now we're fetching all rows all the time, even if not displayed) but it also prevents to have per-provider settings of what rows to disable, concentrating this settings just on one place.

body:
Tests are failing. You need to run pre-commit before pushing.

There also appears to be unrelated changes to the music controller, Jellyfin provider and Claude.md. 

Also I have concerns about the changes to the tracks controller. Plugin/metadata providers now take priority over the track's own music provider for all users, not just those running AudioMuse. That needs discussion before it goes in.

There is also a separation of concerns violation. `radio_playlist` shouldn't know anything about `audiomuse_ai`. author: OzGav
body:
Thanks for the explanation. The goals make sense. The issue is how they're implemented.

Ordering in `radio_playlist`: the problem is your change checks whether the `audiomuse_ai` provider exists, not whether it produced the tracks. Providers must never reference each other by name. Two acceptable approaches: (1) add something generic like `ProviderFeature.ORDERED_SIMILARITY` (or a property on `PluginProvider`) that `radio_playlist` checks on the provider that actually returned the results, or (2) make it a `radio_playlist` config option ("preserve provider order"). Either way `audiomuse_ai` never appears in `radio_playlist` code.

Priority in the tracks controller: your change makes plugin/metadata providers beat the track's own music provider for every user, including people who don't run AudioMuse. That's a behaviour change we can't just slip in. Look at the existing provider priority attribute, maybe respecting that instead of hardcoding the tier order would let users/setup decide, and is worth discussing with Marcel before you rework it.

These are large decisions that you will need guidance from Marcel or Marvin I would say.

As for tests:, you don't need the full suite locally. Run just the relevant files, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/controllers/music/ tests/providers/audiomuse_ai/` . That takes seconds. And `pre-commit run --all-files` catches the lint/format failures before you push.

Also please split the music controller sync fix and the Jellyfin auth fix into their own PRs as they're unrelated and the Jellyfin one reaches into aiojellyfin private attributes, which will break when that library changes.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Thanks - this one targets the actual failure path. I traced the startup log from the issue report myself and the wipe is indeed the universal player restore deleting configs because the squeezelite child rows briefly had `player_type: player` persisted.

The root cause is that `Player.__init__` calls `create_default_player_config` with the constructor-time player type, which for squeezelite is still the class default (`player`) - the real type (`protocol`) is only set later during setup. So every client (re)connect flipped the persisted row and healed it moments later via `update_state`. If registration got interrupted in between (shutdown while clients reconnect, which is exactly what happens on a container recreate), the corrupted row was flushed to disk and the next boot deleted the universal player config.

I pushed a commit to this branch that fixes that root cause: `create_default_player_config` no longer rewrites `player_type` on existing configs - genuine type changes are already persisted by `update_state` after registration. Your restore guard remains useful as defense-in-depth and to heal configs that are already corrupted in the wild, and the deepcopy fix for the summary reads is a nice catch as well.

author: marcelveldt
body: Closing this one in favor of #4634, which addresses the actual cause of the settings loss (see my comment there): the wipe happens in the universal player restore path due to a corrupted persisted `player_type`, not in the in-memory replace path this PR touches - so this change can't fix #5745. The replacement hardening itself isn't wrong (re-hydrating the full config and setting the initialized flag on a replaced player object are real gaps), so feel free to resubmit that separately with an accurate description if you think it's still worth it.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
Hey @silasmariusz,

This afternoon I blocked my calendar to have a play with this. Overall, it works okay. I especially like the sync delay :). Before I do a deep dive into the code, I would like to iterate on the UX first.

## 1 Config options
Currently, when I add the plugin, I get presented with **all** the options which is just too overwhelming for the user. My suggestion is:
- Let's get rid of the non-essential options and just use sane defaults for this For example, do users really need to configure things such as 'Flash rate (hz)', 'Min hold (ms)' and 'Release (ms)' for the strobe?
- Then, with what's left, let's make those options all `advanced` so the user will only see them when they toggle the advance switch
- Then, we can use `depends_on` to only show settings when certain pre-conditions are met. For example, I _think_ the pulse and strobe settings only work when the user picks Club or Pulse mode?
- Per section, we should include [`ConfigType.LABEL`](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/9a3bb40eb7b3d0382c067e1c5443f73d2f17f4d8/music_assistant/controllers/player_queues/config.py#L231) to clearly describe what the section does in terms of lights effects.

## 2 The preview
The preview is a really cool feature. A few notes on usability here:
- Let's not pick 'Music / album colours' as default here. It took me a while to figure out that the metronome does not have any album colours, which resulted in the lights not doing anything
- What is the point of the slides below each light(section) in the preview? Let's clarify this so the user knows what is being changed when changing the slider.

Once we get the UX right, we'll start iterating on the code. I am more than happy to help out with that :)

author: marcelveldt
body:
> * Shouldn't it be named "slimproto" instead of squeezelite?

It was named this way previously but nobody understands what that means. We focus on software based (squeezelite) implementations so we named it that way accordingly.


> * Why players are classified as PlayerType.PLAYER or PlayerType.PROTOCOL? Is it make sense since software players can provide power control too?

Software players can also run other protocols (e.g. airplay on picoreplayer) so those should be marked as protocol only and we only use the player type for actual hardware players here.

> Is it make sense since software players can provide power control too?

We don't support power control for protocols at all and there is also no need. On squeezelite, we send a power ON when the stream starts and OFF when the stream stops.

body:
Well, supporting power control on a protocol is VERY difficult as that is not how we designed the protocols support.
When we tried to implement it, we ran into weird edge cases with multiple protocols and how to decide who wins.
So that is when I decided to simplify it and simple never allow power control on a protocol and fixed the cast implementation to not need a power control anymore to start/stop the cast app. I kind of forgot about the squeezelite implementation where you can have a something wired up to the slimproto power.

So far the only device I have seen in the wild that supports squeezelite as protocol is a WiiM device. 
In all other cases, it would be fine to have squeezelite based players just be the native player themselves.
For the PiCorePlayer case, which can also have airplay as secondary protocol, AirPlay would just become an automatically linked subprotocol of the squeezelite player.

Let me run some tests if we can safely detect if a player is a WiiM device and then flip the whole logic:
A squeezelite player is just a PlayerType.PLAYER unless it is in the exceptions list, instead of the other way around.

author: OzGav
body:
Not quite, regular Google devices aren't affected. The report behind this is a cheap third-party cast speaker (a Terris CCM 283), so being non-Google it gets wrapped by a universal player. The #4406 fix already runs on every cast device, not just groups, but for a wrapped device it was checking the cast's own queue instead of the universal player's, so it always came back "not finished" and the player sat on "playing" forever at the end of the queue. This PR points the check at the correct queue and doesn't change when the recovery is allowed to kick in.

I considered what this PR might break and the answer is basically nothing. The new lookup only applies to wrapped devices, so Google casts, groups and stereo pairs behave exactly as they do today. And a false trigger is as unlikely as it was in #4406, by the time we mark the stream as finished, the device already has all the audio, so if it's still stuck buffering at that point it really is the end of the stream. So far this is only confirmed on this one device, but the fix does nothing unless a device actually gets stuck in that state. The contributor has verified it on the device itself, and the PR includes tests covering the wrapped, native and group cases. On that basis I think this is sound.

author: OzGav
body:
First thing that happened was I had Claude do a command line test. This is the assessment

---------------
Before writing any code I prototyped the ffmpeg side on the command line (ffmpeg 7.1.1) to check the approach was sound.

The problem: afir (the convolution filter) needs two audio inputs — the music and the impulse response — where every other filter we use takes one. There were two ways to feed it: add the IR file as a second -i input and reference it as [1:a], or pull it into the filtergraph as a source using amovie. I tested the amovie approach because it keeps everything inside a single -filter_complex string, so the only thing that has to change is how we build the filter string — not the input arguments or the stream mapping.

Three things I checked:

1. Does it work at all? Fed it an identity IR (one that should do nothing). Output came back identical to the input, same RMS and peak (−24.08/−21.07 dB). So the filter is transparent when it should be and the graph is wired up correctly.
2. Does it actually convolve? Swapped in an echo IR. Output changed as expected (−24.29 vs −24.08 dB), so it's genuinely applying the impulse response rather than quietly passing audio through.
3. What happens on a sample rate mismatch? Ran a 44.1k IR against a 48k stream. No error, exit 0 — ffmpeg negotiates the rate itself. Adding an explicit aresample on the IR made no difference to the output. So mismatched rates aren't a crash or a correctness problem; it's just a question of where we choose to resample for best quality.

That's what gave me confidence the two-input problem fits entirely inside one -filter_complex string, which is why this PR is just the plumbing to build that string, with no convolution feature attached yet.

-----------------------

I also tested to make sure that there was no regression with this branch and all seemed fine. I havent as yet done a full test of the convolution filter as I havent done the frontend changes yet. 

However, tests have also been added as part of this PR and there's a mix of automated tests and one-off checks.

Most of the new tests check that we build the right ffmpeg command as we should still use the simple -af form when every filter is a normal one-in-one-out filter, and only switch to the more complex labelled form when a filter needs a second input. There are tests for a complex filter on its own, one sandwiched between simple filters, and one pulling in more than one extra input.

On top of that there's a test that actually runs ffmpeg rather than just checking the string. It generates a one-second tone plus an "identity" impulse response, one that mathematically should leave audio untouched and runs them through the real command we build, and then measures the output level and checks it matches the input. If the graph were wired up wrong, ffmpeg would either fail outright or the levels wouldn't match. That's the command line check Claude did up front, turned into something that runs every time.

author: marcelveldt
body:
I think this is a bit over-engineered. A much more simple take on this is by simply throwing an exception here (based on MusicAssistantError so its even translatable).

- Throw a timeout error if the provider timed out
- Throw another specific error if fetching the items failed

This will already naturally travel to the frontend today, no additional plumbing needed at all.

Note that we have adjusted the frontend nowadays so it will do separate queries for the global search instead of one big unified one. Frontend does one call to get the library results (very fast) and then subsequent calls per (selected) providers. So this whole flow already works well if you combine it with propagating errors if they arrise. We should just not swallow the errors but convert them to a known error where needed and raise.

author: OzGav
body:
Thanks for the follow-up attempt, but as I see it there is a serious flaw in the retry loop that would cause library data loss. Stepping through what happens:

1. When a sync runs, Music Assistant first makes a list of every file it already knows about from previous scans. It then walks the share to build a second list of every file it can see right now. At the end it compares the two lists and deletes anything from the library that was in the old list but not seen in the new scan. That is how removed files get cleaned up. There are two safety checks before the delete step: the sync stops if the scan reported errors at the top level of the share, and it stops if the scan found nothing at all.

2. Now add your retry loop and imagine the NAS drops out partway through a scan of a big library. The first attempt gets through 130k of 290k files, then the share stops responding and the scan records the error.

3. Your code sees the error, clears the error list, unmounts, waits, and tries again. The second and third attempts do the same. Importantly, the list of files found so far is never reset, so it still holds the 130k files from the first partial attempt.

4. After the third failed try the loop just ends and the sync carries on. At this point the error list is empty, because your retry code cleared it each time, and the "files seen" list holds 130k files.

5. The safety checks now pass when they should not. No errors recorded, so no stop. Files were found, so no stop. The sync moves on to the compare-and-delete step and removes the 160k files it never got to, along with their playlist entries, favourites and play counts.

So if the retries run out, a short NAS outage ends up deleting a large chunk of the library. The current code in dev stops the sync in that same situation and nothing is lost. The comment in your code says the errors are handed back so the sync will stop safely, but the code clears them first, so that never happens. I am surprised you didn't see this in your testing.

There are more problems beyond that one. Because the file lists are kept between attempts, a retry that succeeds will process the same files twice. If the remount itself fails, which is the most likely thing when the server is down, the code throws an error on the first try and the backoff never happens. When the code gives up it leaves the share unmounted, so playback and browsing are broken until the provider is restarted. And the retry only kicks in when the top folder of the share fails to read, while the errors in the original issue were thousands of failures in subfolders, which this code never notices. There are also no tests covering any of this new behaviour.

On the remounting you are doing, it is not needed at all. When an SMB connection drops, the OS does not unmount the share. The mount stays in place and the Linux kernel automatically reconnects as soon as the server is reachable again, using the same credentials. So in the realistic failure case, a NAS that reboots or a network blip, the mount heals itself and there is nothing for Music Assistant to do. Unmounting and remounting while the server is down cannot succeed anyway, and risks leaving the share in a worse state than if it had been left alone.

So the approach here is not correct. The fix should be done higher up in the shared filesystem provider code where it will also benefit all the file system providers. What should happen is the scan should give up quickly once it hits a run of consecutive read errors, instead of grinding through every remaining file at a couple of minutes per failure, which is what turned a ten second outage into days in your case. A scan that had any errors should never run the delete step, so a failed scan can never remove anything from the library. And after a failed sync the provider should retry sooner than the normal sync interval and mark itself available again once a scan succeeds, rather than staying unavailable until someone restarts it. None of that requires touching the mount, and it would protect a local USB drive that disappears mid-scan just the same as an SMB share. I would suggest closing this PR, as the retry-and-remount idea is not salvageable, but a PR along the lines of the above would be welcome. Alternatively, I can work on it.
