author: MarvinSchenkel
context: pr#3843 Add Yandex Alice plugin provider v1.7.4 — Russian voice control via an auto-created Dialogs skill
body:
Thanks for this — it's a genuinely well-engineered provider (constant-time secret/skill_id checks, bounded LRU+TTL state cache, consistent `CancelledError` re-raise, broad test suite). All MA controller calls match real signatures and the earlier SSRF/wrapping comments are addressed. A few things worth resolving before merge:

### 1. Fire-and-forget play/transfer failures are invisible at default log level
`dialogs.py` dispatches `play_for_alice` (~L1252) and `transfer_queue` (~L1093) via `mass.create_task`, whose done-callback only logs task exceptions when `LOGGER.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)`. Alice has already told the user "Включаю…"/"Перевожу…", so a failed `play_media` (bad URI, `PlayerUnavailableError`, unplayable item) is silently dropped at the default log level — "Alice said it played but nothing happened" becomes undiagnosable. `execute_control` already wraps its dispatch in `try/except` + `_LOGGER.exception`; please mirror that around these two calls.

### 2. Stale disambiguation state not cleared from the application tier in some control branches
In `_handle_control`, the generic dispatch branch deliberately clears pending state from both tiers via `_without_pending(app_state_in)` (with an explaining comment), but the `list_players`, `now_playing`, `forget_player`, and `transfer`-success branches return only `session_state` or spread raw `app_state_in`. On screenless Yandex Station devices that don't echo `state.session` back — exactly the surfaces the app-tier fallback exists for — a prior disambiguation prompt can resurface on the next turn. Apply `_without_pending(app_state_in)` consistently across these branches.

### 3. Blocking synchronous file IO on the async config path
`skill_manifest_provider.py` uses `path.read_text()` / `path.stat()` / `write_text()` (L297, L341, L358, L398, L411), reached from the async `get_config_entries` (manifest banner + export/import/reset/validate actions) and one `os.stat` per webhook request via `parse_intent → _resolve`. Practical impact is low (small local files, cached manifest), but it does block the event loop — wrap the filesystem calls in `asyncio.to_thread`.

### 4. Hardcoded Russian strings bypass `strings.json` localization
`export_to_override` / `import_from_paste` / `reset_override` / `validate_override_message` return fully-formed Russian sentences that flow straight into config-UI `label=`, while the rest of the provider localizes via `strings.json`. Non-Russian users see Russian text in the manifest-override (advanced) section. Please move these to translation keys with `{0}`/`{1}` params.

### 5. Public-URL validator doesn't resolve hostnames (DNS-rebinding gap)
`url_helpers.is_public_https_url` only checks IP *literals*; a hostname that resolves to a private/loopback address (or `localhost.` with a trailing dot) passes, and `webhook_probe` would then POST to it. Blast radius is limited (admin-supplied URL, effectively self-SSRF), so this is defense-in-depth — but a connector-level guard on the resolved IP would close it robustly (validation-time DNS resolution is TOCTOU-racy).

### 6. Test-coverage gaps on lifecycle + destructive actions
- No `test_plugin.py` — `YandexAlicePlugin.handle_async_init` / `loaded_in_mass` / `unload` / route registration (the provider lifecycle entrypoint) are untested.
- `test_init_actions.py` exercises only ~4 of ~18 dispatcher branches; the side-effecting ones (`DELETE_SKILL`, `REGENERATE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `CLEAR_AUTH`, `ADOPT_EXISTING`, `TEST_WEBHOOK`, `REFRESH_STATUS`) are never dispatched.
- Untested production logic: `_resolve_genre` / `_resolve_my_wave` success paths, the `enqueue_option → QueueOption` mapping, and the malformed-webhook-body branches in `dialogs.py`.

author: MarvinSchenkel
context: pr#3843 Add Yandex Alice plugin provider v1.7.4 — Russian voice control via an auto-created Dialogs skill
body:
Re-reviewed at `7262bd4`. Thanks for working through the previous round — five of my six earlier points are addressed, and the DNS-rebinding one is addressed better than I asked: `_PublicAddressResolver` validating every *resolved* address in `webhook_probe.py` closes it at the connector layer rather than at validation time, which is the robust version. The test suite is also in much better shape now (333 tests, `test_plugin.py` added, destructive dispatcher actions covered).

One critical and three problems left before this can go in.

### [CRITICAL] Decrypted Yandex auth tokens are returned to the frontend on every settings render

`__init__.py:874` and `setup_view.py:706` build `SECURE_STRING` entries whose `value=` is the plaintext resolved by `_resolve_secure_string_from` (`__init__.py:296`), which falls back to `saved_config.get_value(key)` — and `Config.get_value` **decrypts** `SECURE_STRING` values before returning them.

Masking only happens in `Config.__post_serialize__`, which iterates `self.values`. The `config/providers/get_entries` API command returns a bare `list[ConfigEntry]`, and `ConfigEntry` has no equivalent hook — so nothing masks these. `hidden=True` is a UI display hint and does not affect serialization.

Net effect: the long-lived Passport `x_token` (months-lived, covers the whole Yandex account) and the Dialogs skill OAuth token are sent in plaintext in the API response every time the provider settings page renders. That contradicts the invariant stated in the models code itself:

> drop all password values from the serialized dict. API consumers (including the frontend) are not allowed to retrieve it (even if its encrypted) but they can only set it.

Reading it requires an authenticated `CONFIG_PROVIDERS_READ` session, so this is exposure surface (devtools, HAR exports, browser extensions, logging proxies) rather than privilege escalation — but it's a long-lived credential and the fix is cheap.

**Fix:** keep the decrypted value for internal use during the render, but don't put it on the outgoing entry. `yandex_smarthome/__init__.py:448-469` has the pattern — it echoes only `values.get(...)`, i.e. what the current request already carried, and never reaches into storage for the outgoing `value=`.

### [PROBLEM] `transfer` source player bypasses the exposed-players allowlist

`dialogs.py:1113` passes `default_id` straight through as `source_queue_id`:

```python
self._mass.create_task(
    self._transfer_queue_logged(
        source_queue_id=default_id,
        target_queue_id=target.player_id,
    )
)
```

`default_id` comes from the webhook body (`state.session.last_player_id` / `state.application.last_player_id` / `state.user.preferred_player_id`, computed at `dialogs.py:543`) and is used without validation. The *target* is filtered through `resolve_player_candidates(..., exposed_ids=self._exposed_player_ids)` twelve lines above, and every other control path filters too — only the transfer source doesn't. So a caller can name a player the user deliberately excluded from `CONF_EXPOSED_PLAYERS` and pull its queue onto an exposed one.

**Fix:** resolve `default_id` through `resolve_player_candidates(..., exposed_ids=self._exposed_player_ids)` before using it as `source_queue_id`, matching what the target path already does.

### [PROBLEM] Pending disambiguation state in `application_state` never expires

`pending_command` and `awaiting_query` are mirrored into `application_state` (`dialogs.py:1435`, `dialogs.py:884`), which by design survives session resets, and are read back unconditionally at `dialogs.py:573`. Neither carries a timestamp, and `is_new` never clears them — only an explicit `YANDEX.REJECT` does. The in-process `_state_cache` does enforce a 5-minute TTL (`dialogs.py:398`); the persisted tier has no equivalent.

So an abandoned "which speaker?" prompt sits in `application_state` indefinitely. In a much later, unrelated session, an utterance ending in `на <X>` that happens to match one of the stale candidate names — likely, since those names are the user's own speakers — lets `_try_resume_pending` replay the old query. Alice plays something the user never asked for, in response to a command that may not have been a play request at all.

**Fix:** stamp the state with a timestamp when writing it to `application_state` and age it out against `_STATE_CACHE_TTL_SEC` the same way `_cache_get` does; or clear the pending/awaiting keys whenever `is_new` is true.

### [PROBLEM] `_saved_provider_config` typed `object | None`

`__init__.py:241` returns `object | None`, which forces `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` at both call sites (`saved_config.get_value(...)` / `saved_provider.get_value(...)`). `ProviderConfig` is already imported under `TYPE_CHECKING`, so this can just be `ProviderConfig | None` and both ignores go away.

---

I also have a handful of non-blocking suggestions (blocking `read_bytes` on the skill logo at `auto_create.py:273`, Adopt/Recreate matching an existing Yandex skill by display name alone, `webhook_probe` bypassing `create_clientsession()`'s User-Agent, and `VERSION` 1.7.5 vs the 1.7.4 in the title) — happy to write those up separately, but none of them need to hold up the merge.

Moving to draft while the above is addressed. Ping me when it's ready for another pass.

author: OzGav
context: pr#4919 Add multi channel for local audio
body:
This approach seems viable and worth approving eventually, but as submitted it isn't ready to merge. To get it there I believe it needs:

- An opt-in config toggle because as it stands, every multichannel device starts receiving all content (including plain stereo) as 8-channel PCM on upgrade, with no way to turn it off.
- A defined answer for sync groups, even if that answer is "multichannel disables when grouped". Right now every group member receives the leader's channel count and nothing converts it.
- The device and session channel counts clamped consistently (shared rule, one place). Devices advertising 1 or >8 channels currently get their stream opened at a different count than the session delivers, and 3/4/5/7-channel devices have no channel-order handling.
- The `playback.py` merge redone as lines 1252–1265 resurrect code that #4901 deliberately removed.
- The files cleaned up

Happy to see this land once those are addressed — multichannel output to an AVR is a genuinely valuable capability.

author: marcelveldt
body: GitHub’s official Search issues and pull requests documentation lists no fine-grained repository permission for `GET /search/issues`, and the permission guidance notes that public resources can be accessed without repository permissions. This fallback is explicitly scoped to the public `music-assistant/support` repository; `metadata: read` is mandatory for every GitHub App and is also requested here. Adding `issues: read` would therefore broaden the token without enabling an otherwise unavailable operation, so I’m keeping the narrower traced scope.

author: marcelveldt
body: The documented fallback remains available: `GET /search/issues` does not require the configurable Issues permission for this public-repository search. The job explicitly requests the App’s mandatory `metadata: read` permission, so the matrix reflects the actual endpoint requirement without over-granting `issues: read`.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Music Assistant works by taking a media_player entity (source player) and creating a Queue audio stream.
That source player only receives a raw PCM audio stream or compressed with FLAC, nothing more.
Sending metadata the ordinary way is not possible because the source player (the one actually playing audio) plays a long stream of audio because all transcoding and other audio plumbing is handled by Music Assistant.


Because of the lack of metadata within Home Assistant itself I've created the optional to "spit out" the media player as a separate media_player (prefixed with mass in the entity_id). On that media player the full metadata should be available. If you're missing something, let me know.

One usecase is however not covered in this approach and that is if the actual player want to display something about what it is playing. That metadata is also lost. I've looked at ICY-Meta but that is normally used for radio streams. Not sure if it will also work for a flac/pcm stream.

Another approach could be that I fire an event on the HA eventbus with the media details, for you to pick up ?
Fetching the metadata yourself is also possible, you can access hass.data["mass"] from your custom component to have access to the full Music Assistant instance:

if mass := hass.data.get("mass"):
    queue = mass.players.get_player_queue("media_player.my_player")

Do note that this may break if I change the internals. Maybe an event is better with a predescribed format.

author: marcelveldt
body:
This is called a "race condition" in developers code.
You mount the network location from Home Assistant. At startup, Music Assistant runs a scan for library changes. At that time the network drive is not yet available and thus it fails to find those files. If you wait another 3 hours it will discover them.

I will add a small delay in the initial sync to prevent this from happening.

author: marcelveldt
body:
A spinning wheel means that no image is available (yet) for a media item.
I will change that to some fallback image soon because the spinner is a bit confusing.


**artists**: image/metadata is always retrieved from metadata providers, as long as the artist is matched on musicbrainz.
**albums**: metadata is not retrieved in advance from metadata providers but lazy loaded. If you watch the full details (once) for an album it will fetch all metadata. In case of local files, we'll try to grab the image from the underlying tracks of the album (embedded image in ID3 tag).
**tracks**: same as albums but image is retrieved from embedded image in ID3 tag if present.

author: marcelveldt
body:
This error happens if the queue streamer was not able to fetch the audio stream in time or did not get a response in time from the music provider. As this is all realtime (PCM) audio streaming this might happen if there's a small hiccup etc. I did not implement any retries yet so that can be improved. At the moment it just skips over the track and picks the next one.

So this error can happen if the track is not available due to network issue or its not available on the provider at all.

The ID is indeed an internal ID. The error is now logged just for me as indication how often this happens.
You're saying it happened 142 times in 60 tracks so that feels a bit too much. 

When I'm going to implement the seeking I need to make adjustments to this part of the code (the actual chunk retrieval of provider) and I will make this more robust. I assume you did not notice any audio hiccups ?

Besides that I have plans for a built-in info editor to update the metadata yourself including the images and prioritize those. The backend plumping is already present for that but need to find some time some day to create the UI

body:
I've had the same usecase as you and in the end I settled on another route and just leave the CC powered and instead control the amplifier/speaker connected to it. The CC consumes about 1.2W idle so that is not the whole world.

The more I think of it, the more I think there indeed is a usecase for this in the MA codebase as a simple alternative for the template media player approach. In fact, whole MA can be seen as an alternative for the templated media player.

So this is how I see it:

- Add a setting in MA integration to attach a toggle entity to a media player for power control.
- Add a setting in MA integration to attach another media_player for volume control.
- Any other usecases will not be supported by MA and are considered "very advanced" and must be solved by writing a template mediaplayer in yaml, which in turn can be imported by MA.

I think it's a pretty common scenario (in Home Assistant at least) that a media player is actually powered from a smart plug or something like that or in the case of a streaming device connected to an amplifier. The current way to handle that requires a fair bit of fiddling with yaml.

Other approach would be to just introduce a new helper entity in HA for this task. A simplified GUI based universal media player with the features I mentioned above: Wrap a media player and allow the power and/or volume control to be handled by another device.

To be continued...

author: marcelveldt
body:
The issue is that the same recording can exist in multiple albums. Recording studios do not remaster or re-record it when they place it on another (compilation) album. For the streaming providers I just query which tracks belong to an album and I get the correct listing. In this case (filesystem) I make a query on the database (to prevent accessing the disk) and that's what's causing this issue. A unique track (with same recording id) gets linked to the album that first comes in the db.

So it is in fact the isrc (or recording id) is causing the issue that it should prevent in the first place :-)

Stupid I did not think about that earlier.
I am going to adjust the logic and either query disk to get the real listing or adjust the database model.

I think I'm going with the database model because some people just dump the music files in a random dir.

I'll let you know when there's something to test.

body:
The problem is that I have not been able to reproduce this issue ever nor did it get reported by others. Only difference is that you have a very large music collection on disk.

Even though I'm intrigued by it and I want to know what's going on :-)

The "websocket flooding" messages can be caused by 2 conditions:
1) A rogue component that has an insane amount of state changes and/or events. We're talking about 100s of events in seconds here.

2) A component (HA core or integration) that is doing blocking I/O within the event loop, causing things to lock for 100s of millisonds or even worse, seconds. 

I suspect you are victim of number 2, you have some component (custom integration ?) that is blocking the eventloop from time to time. When the eventloop is locked all actions get stalled, including state changes and event messages. So for example Music Assistant that is doing a scan on your 10.000 songs collection causing an event even 100ms (more or less).

What I do not understand is that we only see the result of that issue and not the issue itself. The HA core is very robust guarded against this kind of pitfalls and even logs integrations that lockup the eventloop.

To be continued...

author: marcelveldt
body:
A song has song artists (or cooperating artists) --> this can be one or more artist(s), I accept some common separators such as the slash and semicolon. 

A song is part of an album, the album has one (and only one) artist. The song artists do not have to be the same as the album artist.
Only the album artist is added by default to the library (which is similar to a favorited artist). Cooperating artists are NOT favorited by default or you will end up with 1000s of artists that might not be your interest.

While browsing the library you can add additional artists/albums/tracks to the library (mark them favorite) with the buttons for that in the interface. So in this case you're browsing the Barcelona album from Album artist Freddie Mercury and you see one track listed with Montserrat Caballé you can add her to your favorite artists too.

Looking at your screenshot above Montserrat is not added as artist to the song/track.
You can put multiple artists in the artist tag with a separator, the most common one is the slash (space slash space) and the semicolon.

The case you're describing is even different (and not so common) where there are multiple (individual) artists on the same album, not being various artists.

I do not support that, the albumartist tag is just treated as 1 single artist.
So the way it is designed now you will see the album "Barcelona" by artist "Freddie Mercury" (or Montserrat Caballé if you picked that as albumartist in the tag) and underlying songs have multiple artists.


![Schermafbeelding 2022-05-23 om 14 34 25](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6389780/169820329-137baefb-01f5-4072-8f39-545722d88997.png)

1) Volume normalization is enabled by default and set to the EBU-R recommendation of -23 LUFS. So yes, audio will sound a bit less loud but benefit is that all audio will have equal loudness. You can disable or increase the normalization gain in the queue settings.

from within the Music Assistant panel, click Queue in the bottom bar. Click the menu button (3 dots top right). Increase the volume level so it better suits the level of other sources you play on the same speaker.

2) That is correct. If you really want the complete metadata shown in your HA interface, you can choose to export the players back to HA but this time including the metadata. We're investigating options to improve this in the future.

3) Seems like a buffering issue. What is your internet connection like ? Can you also observe cpu usage while starting playback of a stream ?

author: marcelveldt
body:
1) You'd be surprised how different all music sounds in the current "loudness war". Normalizing audio according to EBU-R means volume leveling to reach the same perceived loudness. Setting it to -17 means there is enough headroom left. Your sound may actually sound better. The only downside is that you have to turn the volume knob a bitter higher than you're used to.

2) Where else do you want to see what's playing? On the speaker/player/hardware itself is not going to happen I'm afraid. 

3) Both network/internet bandwidth and cpu seem fine to me, that's not the issue. I will try to tune the internal buffer sizes a bit and let you know once I have something ready to test. Do you have the chance to test playback on any other device by any chance ?

An album has one or more album artists

author: marcelveldt
body:
Been testing for a few hours and Kodi behaves really strange when it comes to connecting to a FLAC stream (without duration) and keeps connecting over and over completely ignoring the fact that there is no content length. It even fails to detect the content type from the headers even though it is literally set to "audio/flac".

Even when I ignore the duplicate GET request and get it playing it keeps connecting over and over with multiple requests for no reason. Only when I serve a file with an actual duration it calms down and it accepts the request. Point is that a FLAC stream of no duration is served, just like an online radio stream. So I decided to monitor Kodi (debug log turned on) while connecting to a random radio stream from internet. Guess what, same behavior. Duplicate HEAD request, GET request and a final GET request including a request for ICY metadata. So there is an implementation error in Kodi undetected. The details should have been grabbed in the first HEAD request. 

Anyways.... If somebody want to discuss that with the Kodi devs that's probably the best solution as it is a broader issue and not just with MA. Difference is that MA disconnects the stream on that second GET request.
It's even worse because once the stream actually is playing (both MA and radio streams have this issue), Kodi keeps sending a HEAD request every 30 seconds or so. Don't know why it does that but that does seem to me like a waste of resources without HTTP2 multiplexing or maybe this is for some reason I do not think about now.

I'll implement a (hopefully temporary) workaround in the code. If the user agent matches Kodi/OSMC I will ignore the first GET request and only start the stream on the second. I'll pass in some silence in the first request just to not upset the whole thing.

My feeling of what is wrong is that Kodi is trying to fetch the duration from the actual stream, hence the first GET request.
That duration is not going to be there because it is an "endless" FLAC stream. I even tried instructing ffmpeg to write a duration of 48 hours but that is not possible as it seems.

Please test the fix/workaround in next 2022.6.5 patch release.
Thanks!

author: marcelveldt
body:
This is the behavior I observed with Kodi clients:
head request
head request
get request without icy metadata header
get request without icy metadata header
get request with icy metadata header

The client "sticks" at the last request and keeps playing but this all happens within 2 seconds so it's all very time sensitive.

Music Assistant want to start the stream once the client is connected (or multiple clients if multiple should receive the stream). The existing behavior (that works with all players except Kodi) is that it starts streaming audio chunks once the client is connected (GET request). In the HEAD request only the contenttype is shared.

Kodi tries to probe the file to receive additional details it is not going to get.
It should have read the headers telling it is content-type "audio-flac" and the fact that there's a chunked header tells Kodi not to do any range requests (which it does).
I'm assuming here Kodi wants to know more (duration perhaps?) and tries to fetch the file once to grab those details.

Once it actually gets through all hurdles and is playing, it plays amazingly well and even display what is playing thanks to the ICY metadata.

I don't know if this probing thingie is something only happening once. If so I could create a special static endpoint for the Kodi clients instead of the current randomly generate stream url (to invalidate any cache).
Another option is to be even more forgiving on the number of requests and timeout.

Big problem here is I can't differentiate between a misbehaving client and Kodi.
I don't want to delay the start of chunks streaming too much as it ill delay the entire experience. Imagine you have to wait seconds when you're seeking in a file etc.

The matcher is very strict to prevent wrong versions being matched. By default it matches on unique id's such as the **isrc** or the **musicbrainz id**. So if the isrc is in the ID3 tags it will use that to match.

As a last resort a match is made on an exact name match. In that case the track artist, album, title and version must exact match. I agree the case match is maybe a bit too strict so I'll adjust that and consider this a bug ;-)

No, Music Assistant connecting to another Music Server (Like Plex, Emby, LMS etc.) will probably never be implemented as MA is considered a (Music-only/focused) alternative for those. But you never know. If it receives much user votes, never say never....

The other way around, MA being a (DLNA) source for those Media Servers is more likely to happen.
In that case the music collection lives in MA and it can share that with the other platforms, just like it can send playback to supported platforms now.

If you want your music in MA, connect it to your streaming provider(s) or make sure it can access the local files.
Development focus for MA will be in extending the features and have more music providers supported, including a way to directly connect a NAS/remote file location instead of mount workarounds.

author: marcelveldt
body:
I'm not sure if I can fix this... Your receiver seems to be caching ahead the audio data and instead of displaying the "icy" metadata of the currently playing track, its displaying whatever it has buffered. That's a serious design flaw for such a big brand.

The ICY metadata is encoded with the stream, the same way as online radio stations do this.
So we send one long stream of audio from MA. Every x bytes, there's a metadata chunk about the audio being sent.
The only difference is that online radio stations are live so you can't buffer ahead more than a few seconds tops while MA allows you to cache ahead whatever you need/ For example Sonos caches about 5 minutes ahead.

I can put a small guard in the code to prevent the player from buffering more than a full track ahead but that might harm other players performance so I need to think about this a bit more.

Maybe you better set the audio stream to FLAC instead ?
That will most probably disable the metadata but you get better audio quality in return.
You can change the audio stream to FLAC from the HA settings --> integrations --> Music Assistant --> devices --> pick the MA device for your receives --> See the config entity there where you can select the stream type.

author: marcelveldt
body:
@OzGav if the info is not present locally (as in real files on disk), MA will query metadata providers for that info.
This is done in a "lazy" manner so when you click an artist/album/track for the **first time** (or play it), it will return quickly with the "lazy" object without all metadata present and in the meanwhile a background process will fill in the blanks and upgrade the artist/album/track object in the db with all metadata it can find online, this is the part where also the "track linking" takes place meaning an object from multiple musicproviders get linked.

The only thing it (currently) doesn't do is refresh the interface when it is done grabbing the full object.
I had that before but that UX was also a bit weird where you were looking at some info and several seconds later (or more on slow connections), the page refreshes and there is additional info.

So I'm a bit in doubt to what behavior is best here. 
If you click an item for the first time you get to see whatever info is present on the musicprovider. So for files on disk this means info from ID3 tags and/or images/nfo in the folder structure and for streaming providers whatever metadata the provider has to offer, mostly just the thumbnail but some (e.g. Qobuz) offer really rich metadata already at this stage.

If the item is added to the database, all other info is retrieved and you get a much richer experience.

- This metadata is not retrieved beforehand (at library sync) because it slows the scanning down too much and because it causes a real burden on those metadata providers, which are also community projects which have to pay for their server costs with donations.

- I'm thinking about a background task that slowly loads the missing metadata into the db 

- I'd like to hear some opinions about refreshing the UI once full info is loaded

Because after the "full metadata fetch" the listings will also include the objects of all providers.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> Marcel - note that the issue can be reproduced by yourself by looking at the non mass media_player as that displays the rolling list of tracks - it's not really anything to do with the denon as it is simply displaying the same information that the media_player entity displays. Thanks

No, the non-mass player can't display any metadata because it simply is not there.
Each player controlled by MA just gets one long stream of audio (the queue stream).
The only one that knows what is actually playing at what moment is MA itself and it provides that info in the "mass players" it creates within HA itself. Another way is if the player actively requests (and supports) "icy metadata" which is metadata embedded into the long stream.

In your case the stream type is set to mp3 which more or less also defaults the icy metadata on your receiver I guess
So it is your receiver actually sending that metadata back to HA...

That's why I proposed to just disable the ICY metadata by setting your receiver to receive FLAC which is also better quality (lossless) and most probably your receiver will not request ICY for a flac stream

author: marcelveldt
body:
Cast is very sensitive to errors and the cast integration in HA even more. Sending more than one command at once and the whole socket connection drops off already. It's a real nightmare and it seems that things are getting worse. Other player platforms like Sonos, DLNA and slimproto do not have these issues at all so it must be something in the HA cast integration triggered by MA (or maybe the issue is there always but MA triggers it somehow). 

Today I ran some tests streaming media from a standalone controller casting audio to a cast group in Hires audio (just to stress it a bit more), worked like a champ. Starting the stream from HA (even without MA) caused the socket error from time to time and even worse a lot of hiccups in the audio. Bizarre thing is that at time of those hiccups a socket error pops up in HA as if the socket connection is locking up the cast device itself.

I think there's some flaw going on with the cast platform but I like to do some more tests and maybe even find the cure.
Music Assistant puts a lot more stress on the devices then starting some low quality online audio stream or spotify connect sesssion so I think it just triggers an issue already lingering in the background.

Strange thing is that for the past 3 years MA was a standalone project consuming pychromecast itself to control cast players and that worked perfectly fine after I discovered to treat the socket connection with great care.
I think I'm going to borrow some of my old code to interface with the cast speakers to see if that calms down the annoying issues.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> With 2022.7.0 the pending errors are back as well. I know not directly MA, but indicates high stress on the system:

Not exactly... Those errors can occur i f there are simply too many messages (e.g. when you have too many devices sending state changes for example or MA initial scan shouting a lot of "media changed!" events.
But... you need to have A LOT of messages to make that happen or a really slow client device.

This error can also occur if something is locking up the eventloop, even for a short while.
Home Assistant (and Music Assistant) is written in async python but sometimes do need to interact with oldskool synchronous libraries or functions, such as Google cast. If such interaction is not properly executed in a "executor", this sync code will temporary block the main eventloop and thus stalling everything that is happening.

Both HA core and MA core is 100% async code only and the small amount of sync code is run in an executor.
So, my feeling is that there is some component commonly in HA/MA with an undetected I/O lock issue. The common identifier so far seems to be cast. 

A very clear indicator of my feeling sits in that "pychromecast.error.PyChromecastError" where the chromecast was not able to play music from the stream sent to it. At that time the pychromecast itself locked the eventloop causing MA to fail to stream. A chicken and the egg situation.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Why do you want to serve the audio stream on https and overcomplicate stuff like this ?
This base url is NOT for the api or web interface, its for the audio stream which needs to be **as simple as possible**, so avoid local dns names and avoid https. It works maybe in your setup but I can guarantee you that a lot of players will not like this.

For example google cast players have the google dns servers hardcoded and will never be able to resolve internal dns names. That is why the stream service is hosted on its own as-simple-as-possible http port, otherwise I could have proxied it on the HA webserver. I did that for a reason.

So, I'm not a big fan of making this configurable because it will cause more support to handle and it will most likely not work in a lot of situations. Maybe some sort of hidden environmental variable that nobody knows about ;-)

What's wrong with opening a tcp port in your LOCAL network ?
Let alone all dns issues, why add the overhead of https to the audio stream which is local only ?

author: marcelveldt
body:
I have given a very detailed answer here:
https://github.com/music-assistant/hass-music-assistant/discussions/794#discussioncomment-3331209

This is not about running Home Assistant web interface behind reverse proxy etc. it has nothing to do with a web interface.
We are talking about the audio stream service here, yes that is http but that is all it is, the protocol. 

There are very good reasons to host that on HTTP only and avoid dns lookups.

I'm fine with an undocumented ENV variable to override the base URL if you are willing to take the risks of slower seek times, buffer issues, audio dropouts etc. I simply won't support it because after 3 years working on this project my conclusion is that playback just works most reliable if there's no https or dns lookup involved.

Undocumented because I'd rather tell experienced guys like you that the setting exists than having to support people who use this setting in the wrong way if you get what I mean. Or maybe document it and link to my rant linked above about my choices to host this on a separate port ;-)

I hope you get what I mean. It's not that I do not want to support your setup but I just know it's going to cause trouble. Maybe not for you because you're in luck but it will for others.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Did not yet read into the whole history (just got back from holidays) but a few things are important to know (and remember):

1) Each player has its own settings for player specific settings like stream format, max sample rate etc.

2) If you group a player in Sonos it does not create a special group (like cast does) but it simply designates the first player as "master" player and appends childs to it which will output the same music stream.

3) In relation to the above, if a Sonos player is grouped to another player (so it is a "child" of another player), it no longer has any playback controls of its own, no queue of its own etc. The MA interface tries to make that effect very visible by just hiding all child players underneath the parent player.

4) Unlike the cast ecosystem, Sonos speakers can not be in a group (or multiple groups even) and still have standalone control.

5) While the MA interface visually shows the effect of the grouping, the HA interface does not because its a flat hierarchy.
If you send play command to multiple grouped Sonos players at once you will end up with a bad experience because the default behavior is to redirect any playback related command to the parent/master player.

Maybe we should introduce Music Assistant groups which can dynamically join speakers to a Sonos speakergroup only when needed (and that group is addressed). Turning "off" the group, will dissolve the Sonos speakergroup. So in fact replicating the cast behavior for Sonos (or any speaker brand).

author: marcelveldt
body:
The commands should already be redirected to the "sync master" by default in both MA and the HA core integration but we could have missed a few spots. Another bad thing that may happen is if your scripts address multiple Sonos players at once while they're actually grouped. That may result in the "master" player receiving the same command multiple times.

I need to take a look if I can filter out that second situation. So if a playback related command is received, targeted at multiple players at once, filter out duplicates.

I saw some log warnings from you that a stream request was received multiple times, that is exactly the kind of situation I'd expect to happen when the same command is redirected multiple times.

I'll chew on this a bit and let you know once I have something to test.

Music Assistant launches its own -internal only- webserver to serve the audio stream to players on the local network on TCP port 8095. The ip-address that is communicated to players is derived from whatever you fill in at the "internal URL" field of the HA config. So it only takes the IP-address from there (and even resolves dns if needed) and ignores everything else.

So in your case this is already configured correctly. In your case the log is a strong indication that it is already using the correct IP: "Got stream request for already running stream" means that the player is actually requesting the stream (so it reached the webserver) but it fails after that.

Looks like the Symfonisk speaker is not reachable by the Sonos integration, hence all those ReadTimeoutErrors.
Maybe simply restart the speaker to make it work again?

Another cause of issues could be if you group Sonos speakers and you target multiple speakers at the same time.
If a Sonos speaker is grouped, send playback command to the "parent" speaker. In a future version of MA we will resolve these issues with grouping and make grouped speakers a more first class citizen of the whole experience.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
Yep. So basically YouTube music doesn't have an official api for us to get
our data. We try to mimic the YouTube Music app and parse the results as
best as we can. Unfortunately these results are very inconsistent and might
change from one day to another. This results in occasional weird errors
like the one you are describing.

Luckily for us we use a library that does most of the heavy lifting in
terms of parsing YouTube music data. This library is also frequently
updated to stay in sync with any YouTube music changes. However, MA is
currently implemented as a python package within HA, making it really
difficult for us to pin down version numbers of external libraries we rely
on, like the one described above. This makea it practically impossible to
trace these kinds of errors, because there could be a 1000 reasons (old
library version, incompatible library version, YT Music app changed etc.)
As of MA 2.0, MA will run in a sandboxed environment, making it possible
for us to pin versions of libraries properly. This will make it easier to
reproduce and trace these kind of errors.

Again, I wanna emphasize that YouTube Music doesn't have an office API,
which means 0 guarantees for compatability. Errors like these are expected
to happen, now and in the future. Google might decide to change their
webapp tomorrow, resulting in errors like these. I've even seen cases of AB
testing by Google where one user had a different web app than another user.
So theoretically, with the exact same MA code, one user might get errors
while the other one doesn't.

It's something we probably have to deal with since I don't expect Google to
release an official YouTube music API anytime soon, if ever.

author: marcelveldt
body:
The new version of Music Assistant will run as a standalone application. The reason for this is exactly why it broke now, you can not have two captains on one ship. Both Home Assistant and Music Assistant are very large and complicated projects and it was a very bad idea of me in the first place to run the "core" of Music Assistant within Home Assistant itself.

The 2.0 approach is that the Music Assistant core runs on its own and the Home Assistant integration is just a connector, making it resilient to the kind of dependency issues that killed the v1 version.

For some this may sound as bad news but it is actually very good news because now we can have a much more fine grained control over the players and playback. You already see the first results of this in the early 2.0 betas: Full metadata is displayed.

There is still a lot of work to do on the 2.0 code but his feels like a very strong foundation to continue and make it into something awesome.

### Running the Music Assistant 2.0 BETA

**Preferred method: Home Assistant Add-on**
By far the most convenient way to run the Music Assistant Server is to install the Music Assistant Add-on:

Add the Music Assistant repository to your Home Assistant instance.
Install the Music Assistant add-on.
[Add repository on my Home Assistant](https://github.com/music-assistant/home-assistant-addon)

**Alternative method: Docker image**
An alternative way to run the Music Assistant server is by running the docker image:

```
docker run --network host ghcr.io/music-assistant/server
```

You must run the docker container with host network mode and the data volume is /data. If you want access to your local music files from within MA, make sure to also mount that, e.g. /media. Note that accessing remote (SMB) shares can be done from within MA itself using the SMB File provider.

body:
If music is stuttering it is in 99% of the cases network (bandwidth) or performance (cpu power) related.
Be aware that MA is aimed to provide the best quality of playback and so has a somewhat heavier load on both cpu and network/bandwidth then HA, especially considering the fact that the stream is provided by MA itself.

So take a look at your network, is the connection speed OK (especially 2,4 Ghz WiFi is poor for music streaming) and have a look at cpu and memory usage of the machine running HA/MA.

Normally speaking it should run just fine on a pi 4 with 2gb or more and a descent network connection.

What is strange is that cast is not working out of the box, it is very rare that does not work with a plain network setup like yours. Is your HAOS network config setup with DHCP for both IPv6 and IPv4. ?

Just to confirm: I may hope your HA box is connected to ethernet and not WiFi ?

Note that actual squeezebox hardware is getting sparser everyday, its an aged platform. MA focusses more on the software alternatives like squeezelite and the esp32 incarnation of it.

author: marcelveldt
body:
I know some of the MA users have the WiiM Pro and that runs buttersmooth. So we're back at networking.

All this can impact/hinder mdns traffic badly:

- multicast "enhancements" on WiFi networks => turn it OFF
- fast roaming --> works not well with a lot of IoT devices => turn it OFF
- multicast dns or(mdns forwarder) => malforms packets => turn it off
- igmp snooping => should help multicast traffic but sometimes hurts


These protocols based on multicast are designed for regular domestic networking, not for enterprise like setups.
Best to turn off all enhancements features to make it as dunb as possible and then turn on by one to find out the cause.

author: marcelveldt
body:
In general, I wouldn't recommend turning off the volume normalization because there are so many different loudness levels , especially if you play music from different sources. We use an integrated loudness level based on the EBU-R128 standard and only adjust gain of the entire track up or down so there is no compression of dynamic range. For that same reason of not loosing dynamic range we do not use a limiter and it's the user's responsibility to use sane values for the target level of the volume normalization. 

That said, we should probably add a few warnings if a value higher than -17 is used, because that can indeed lead to clipping if the measurement was not accurate or a wrong default was assumed.

author: marcelveldt
body:
All tracks are processed as raw pcm by Music Assistant internally. So everything you play will be first converted to just raw pcm in the sample rate and bit depth of the origin (unless flow mode is enabled) and the gain adjustment is done while extracting the raw source media so the pcm chunks we get into the streaming engine have the gain adjustment applied, that way there should be enough headroom withit the 16 or 24 bits bit depth Converting to 32 or 64 bits floating point is something I have considered but not worth the overhead and comes at the risk of dithering when going back from 64 bits to 16 or 24 bits so instead I settled on applying the correction gain while extracting the raw audio from its base codec.

All further processing in MA is done at PCM raw audio level, such as the optional equalizer (in the future maybe some room correction or other filters) - if "flow mode" is enabled crossfading is also done on the raw pcm chunks but that will upsample all audio into one static sample rate and bit depth to create one "flow" of audio to send to the player.

The final part in the chain is that MA sends either the raw pcm data to the player or encodes it into a coec of the user's choice, by default this is FLAC due to it being lossless while keeping a sane file size

author: marcelveldt
body:
> @marcelveldt Thanx for all this detailed information and insights. So when i disable volume normalization i will get the original uncompressed flac file from deezer without any volume correction applied. I could not hear any clipping and everything sounded perfectly fine! Thanx for your great work!!!

Not exactly, as explained above MA always processes all audio content in PCM internally so audio is always decoded and optionally any processing is applied. If you have applied FLAC as the output codec to your player this would theoretically mean that a track is decoded and then re-encoded again but as long as a lossless codec is used, there is no loss of quality at all.

And for the record: FLAC is compressed, its just lossless compressed. Formats like MP3 are lossy compressed.

Like explained above I would really recommend to leave volume normalization enabled and not turn it off. Instead change the target volume if you may experience clipping. I'll look into Deezer because I have never ever experienced any clipping with any of the other providers.

If you only play audio from one single source (e.g. Deezer) and that audio source already has normalized its audio files, then its safe to disable normalization in MA. If you play audio from different sources or audio is not normalized at the source, I really recommend to leave normalization enabled for the best experience.

We implemented slimproto in its base/pure form to work with squeezelite as that is the only thing currently still available. I cant test any of the real squeezebox hardware anymore because it is simply not available anymore, even on the 2nd hand shops they're getting sparse or expensive even.

I'm considering splitting up our squeezebox/slimproto integration into a standard version and advanced version where the basic version is our pure, leightweight slimproto implementation in pure python to control squeezelite based players and the advanced just connects to an existing LMS server so you can run LMS and MA side by side and MA just sends commands to the LMS server. We could even just allow for a situation where we host/wrap the LMS server in case somebody does not want to maintain a LMS server.

I'd like to get a few opinions here how people think about this. I also have no idea how popular the good old squeezebox hardware still is among the MA community.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> The reason im sticking to UPnP is to send better quality in terms of Audio Quality to my Sony TV.
> 
> Chromecast has a limit cap on transfering Audio Quality.
> 
> I does sound better.

You will really not be able to hear the difference...
Chromecast is capped to 96khz/24 bits HI-RES audio while DLNA theoretically supports 192/24 but it depends on ythe player. Nobody can hear the difference between (lossless!) 44.1/16 and 48/24, let alone any higher. If you can hear a difference, then you must see a doctor ;-)

What CAN actually be happening is that your device is hurting the audio, for example throwing away bots from an 24 bits source signal instead of dithering and whatnot. Consumer devices like TV's are not exactly meant to produce high quality audio so the firmware designers of those devices usually don't give a damn about audio quality, especially not hi res.

Chromecast on TV's is usually limited to the video version of chromecast (no hi res, 48/16 capped) while the audio version of Chromecast (built in to speakers and receivers) supports 96/24, so super high quality audio.

In your case you are saying that playing to the DLNA player doesn't work from MA.
Well, by default MA sends the lossless FLAC stream to the player but a lot of players can only accept MP3 (or other lossy codecs) on the DLNA interface. 

So long story short, your TV does not support lossless (FLAC) audio in the DLNA interface, you should use cast instead.
Or Airplay, which is also lossless (but limited to redbook 44.1/16 quality) but again, nobody can hear the difference between a proper lossless 44.1/16 bits stream versus any higher sample rates or bit depth, unless maybe on some 40K speakers some good trained ears will hear it, but certainly not on your TV.

You WILL be able to hear a difference between a lossy codec such as MP3 and lossless cd quality.

body:
I've decided that I'm not going to have a lot of focus on trying to support these ancient players natively in MA.
I have looked at the LMS source code and its an awful history of player specific quirks. These players should honestly belong to a graveyard as there are so much better alternatives nowadays. Its maybe a bit rude from me to say it this way but come on, we're talking about almost 20 years old hardware here with limited CPU's, memory etc.

I think people with the real hardware squeezebox devices should not be using MA at all but stick with LMS, its designed for that and includes every possible fix introduced in last 20 (!!!) years for all the hardware players. And its doing a really great job at that. Its UI feels like a throwback into the 90's but its robust and stable.

I feel stupid that I actually start working on this trying to reinvent the wheel of LMS. 

Instead I will only focus on squeezelite from now on and its incarnations in e.g. picoreplayer etc.
I might even rename this player provider "slimproto / squeezelite" to make it very clear its only purpose/focus is support for squeezelite based players.

Next to that I will have a look if we can just create an LMS player provider for MA so that MA talks to LMS.

Let's leave this issue open for now. I'll give an update as soon as I have the LMS player provider ready.

PS: In the meanwhile we have also incorporated support for snapcast in the MA codebase and its sync protocol is so much smoother than slimproto ;-)

author: marcelveldt
body:
Another update. A short track on single repeat was just bound to fail. The squeezelite player has a buffer of about 10 seconds and loads the clip (super fast) into memory, then asks the server for a next track but that has no idea that the player even started playing already because the request comes in only a few milliseconds after actually sending the request to start playback. Its a good old race condition. The MA server is optimized to allow players to buffer more for smoother playback while LMS tends to be a bit slower so the race condition trips not as easy there but it also does exist.

I have put in a bandaid in the code and in my testing its now working fine.

Then to the next issue. The volume normalization was not working correctly on this brown noise audio clip because the limiter would exceed the bounds (the clip has a super high dynamic range) - I have now optimized our code to auto detect this and dynamically adjust the target loudness level to account for more headroom. The file might play crappy the first time but then the measurement is received and it will use the adjusted values in the subsequent runs. 

So, long story short, the issues should be solved in the next update.

1) The first time you play a file like this (which is really bad recorded btw!) - it will have some difficulties to to the huge peaks vs low baseline but the subsequent runs of this file will run in lineair mode and should then run fine from now on. LMS doesn't do EBU based volume normalization but just plain old replay gain, it can not be compared.

I have identified the ffmpeg loudnorm filter acting up on this brown noise file while in the first pass (dynamic mode) but it should be fixed once it has a measurement collecte din the db and do any second phase runs (so any time you play the track after the first run). At least in my case when I test with your file it sounds good and no more muffled pulsing sounds.

The other way I can think of is just detecting these sound effects files and completely disable volume normalization when we detect these. This can be as simple as adding something to the ID3 tags.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Our entire enqueing logic is not really optimized for gapless repeat of short sound effects as we're built with music in mind. I will have another look if I can improve it without making the code too horrible.

Having gapless repeat for the entire queue (even with just one track in it) is something I'm not going to support as its much cleaner and maintainable to just restart the queue. Its also considered such an edge case of an edge case I don't think I should spend energy on it.

What should work is a continuous, gapless repeat of a single track but its a bit player dependent as we already figured out. MA does not only support slimproto (like LMS) but needs to support all modern protocols and player types so its a bit more of a challenge sometimes to satisfy everybody. For example we focus on having large buffers and allow players to buffer as much ahead as they want/can which prevents glitches/artifacts so the best possible playback of MUSIC is ensured.

That does not play well with super short audio clips on repeat where the player itself already filled its buffer before we can even think of feeding a next track.

Long story short, I will have another look at the repeat single track scenario.

Can you confirm that playing the brown noise file on next attempts has no more  muffled sound ?

author: marcelveldt
body:
To sum up this issue. The Music Assistant container (or HA add-on) crashes on some older generation (Intel?) hardware when using the Sonos provider (which in turn uses the Soco python library), most likely due to some dependency (like one of the xml libraries) using CPU instructions not available on older gen x86 CPU's.

The crash seems to already happen as soon as the soco library is imported but we're not 100% sure about that.

Its really hard for us to exactly track what's going on without actual access to such hardware and the specific conditions.
Its a bit searching for a needle in some haystack. We will keep this issue open (and pinned) so people will at least know about this and they can choose to not use the Sonos provider. We have adjusted the code in Music Assistant that nothing will be imported when you did not add a provider to MA.

So workaround for now: Do not use the Sonos provider in MA when you run into this issue.
Longer term solution is going to be that we will switch away from the soco library in favor of the new Sonos api.

author: marcelveldt
body:
The favorite flag (heart icon) in Music Assistant itself is just a way to prioritize your items in the MA library/database, see it as an additional filter. It has no impact on the actual provider but it is true that the streaming providers library content get imported with the favorite flag set to true by default (while filesystem items do not) - this is just some historical decision.

Imo the only proper way to handle it is to allow you per provider(instance) to configure if/how you want to import/export.
This is the item on the backlog we should pickup:

https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/projects/2/views/1?pane=issue&itemId=62335206

author: marcelveldt
body:
You need other scrapers to save the artwork locally in your folders.
Music Assistant always prefers local artwork and metadata but it has to exist. If it doesn't exist, it will query the metadata providers and it will only do that on (first) access. It will not do that proactively as we simply do not have the money to pay for such heavy api access.

There is however a feature request to automatically save any local artwork in the folders so maybe that will one day see the light. Until then my recommendation is to use a a tool like Lidarr or alikes if you want to have all that artwork and metadata saved to your music folders.

That said; focus back on the bug report.
Both you and @OzGav mention that you experience artwork dissapearing. So it has been scraped (and visible in the UI) and then all of a sudden its gone again. Actually this morning I fixed a bug I accidentally ran into that may explain this behavior. So I'd like to ask if this issue still manifests itself in the next version; We will provide a 2.0.7 patch release later today or tomorrow.

author: marcelveldt
body:
The Plex API for music items is.... not great... It misses info such as Album artists and disc and track numbers.
Important info that is needed for matching and presenting the right info. I'll see if I can patch some more bandaid into the Plex provider again but its getting harder and harder for me to recommend the Plex provider if you care about your music.

Don't get me wrong, I really like Plex and I use it daily but for music its just plain crap, its entire datamodel is based around movies and tv shows and they tried to squeeze music in there. Maybe it works ok-ish in their own apps (where they probbaly worked around the quirks) but for an external party talking to their api this is not so great.

If anybody wants to help with improving the Plex provider please contact us as we currently do not have an active maintainer on it and me and the other MA core devs are maintaining it on a best-effort base.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> As a side note : as a developer I would take a long hard look at my database design when noticing it takes Hass so awful long to get rid of all the info associated with a certain music provider upon deleting the latter. I dare say that with an optimised design such operations could be almost instantaneous ...

Works is in the progress for further optimizing. The design is rather complex due to all the provider linking and relation so we choose the safe way on removals which is bad for speed. We're even hitting some sqlite limitations. We get some help from database experts but their time is also limited for contributing to an open source project. So unless you are willing to PR some optimizations I'm going to ignore your comment here ;-)

There may still be bugs in there but that I can influence and fix. I can fix the Plex API if you know what I mean.

I will at least put a patch in the code for the disc/track numbers (and just ignore the zero numbered ones) in Plex but there is only so little we can do.

> DLNA would be a better alternative for MASS, as it increases the reach beyond just Plex based music libraries, and is music savvy. author: marcelveldt
body:
Oh crap what an edge case - who on earth decided its a good idea to just assign the same unique id to multiple parts ?!!
Why not postfix it with something.

Note that you can have multiple ISRC's per track as one recording can have multiple releases (per country/catalog etc).
I'm going to have a good think about how to handle this but for now I would recommend you to simple remove the ISRC's from the music so its not used for matching at all anymore.

author: marcelveldt
body: Question: would the title and/or track number differ in these cases ? Because we could consider adding an additional sanity check and only accept ISRC match if there is a secondary match as well, such as title or disc number

author: marcelveldt
body:
Ah yes that is a good idea. So the MusicBrainz Recording ID IS in fact different then in this case?
But we already have that check in place. We consider musicbrainz id's as a strong identifier so if that is present in both A and B and differs, it will reject the match. Problem is that that code is in the same comparison as isrc and whoever wins, wins.

So we need to make a difference between the 2 here
https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/de95ebf314576d566b00beb982c26380a3af8cde/music_assistant/server/helpers/compare.py#L116

MusicBrainz ID match --> STRICT = reject if both present and A != B
ISRC match --> SOFT MATCH = requires one other soft match like title or whatever

And then we need to make sure that the strict ID match is always executed before the soft match

Can you follow and do you agree ?

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
Just to be super clear here, the delay is caused by **resolving a stream url for a track**, not playing back the actual audio from a given stream url. There's a lot of decryption and cipher magic happening in the background that involves downloading youtube source code to figure out decryption keys. This is CPU intensive and might explain why we are seeing higher delays on other systems. Once the url is resolved, the stream url itself starts instantly.

We could pre-fetch a couple of stream urls that are in the active queue, but this requires a change in the logic of handling the queue and only has a positive effect on YT Music, since it is not required for any other music providers. @marcelveldt any thoughts on this?

Does it actually play that 2 seconds (so do you hear music) ?
Because most often of playback doesn't start and fails this way, it means that the communication with the player failed.

So make sure the players are on the same subnet, no weird network filtering in between etc.

available is NOT a global flag but an indication if the item is available - streaming providers are annoying and sometimes switch their content due to licensing and that can make an item to become unavailable, which we resolve with track linking.

Anyways, setting the available flag from provider availability on the item's available flag is a hack. It is just for api consumers and should not merge with internal logic, hence if we move it to the serialize logic it will be fixed.

You manually disabled the provider.

author: marcelveldt
body:
We currently use ffmpeg/ffprobe as our primary tag reader but it has some issues with mp3 files where it simply doesnt read some of the tags, hence eyed3 is only used to fill in the blanks for mp3 files only. We are considering just switching to a different tag library completely, such as taglib or mutagen but the hard thing is that none of them are async friendly (so we still need to run in an executor) and full support for all tags and filetypes is also hard, that is why ffprobe was so great.

I guess we can swap it around. Use a more robust tag scanner for all common file formats and use ffprobe only for the obscure ones. I am definitely going to look into tinytag, maybe we can even make it async friendly

author: marcelveldt
body:
Without actual access to the device I'm afraid there is nothing I can do here. DLNA is a shitty protocol with shitty implementations by manufacturers that don't give a crap about standards/interoperability. Therefore I do not provide any support for DLNA other than best effort and if you may run into issues you'll have to submit a PR yourself.

Foobar2000 is an application that exists for 2 decades already and has all kind of special device-specific treatments.
In this case making this work would involve comparing wireshark traces of what foobar is sending against what MA sends, its that awful.

The best advise I can give in this situation is to use a streaming protocol other than DLNA. For example hook up a raspberry pi or esp32 board running squeezelite (slimproto), airplay or snapcast which also gives you the benefit of synced playback.
Or a less-DIY and better sounding option is something like a Wiim Pro Plus, Sonos Port or Bluesound Node. Anything other than crappy DLNA with all its quirks.

Don't get me wrong, we also have success stories with DLNA where people are incredible happy with it but looks like you are on the less lucky side.

author: marcelveldt
body:
You are mixing two things here completely...

**temporary sync group:**
You have one player playing and you simply join/unjoin players to it to let other players play the same music.

**permanent sync group:**
This can be seen as a preset to join players together, it will automaticlaly create the syncgroup for you under the hood with a static or dynamic group leader.
You create a group from the MA interface (and that will hold the queue). you can power players within that group if you want them to play or not. Look at the settings of the group as it has some interesting settings for you. 

Looks like you are now mixing up the two.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> After all of this, it is still unclear why we are taking about privileged mode here in this issue. Again, I'm not an expert, so I welcome someone to educate me, but my understanding is that privileged mode is not about file system permissions within the container, but about elevated privileges to access certain apis and devices on the host.

We require privileged mode for the SMB provider, otherwise mounting of samba shares fails. It could be that it also caused other trouble in the past without it enabled but I'm not sure. Most important is the host networking, so that the multicast mdns/upno traffic works out of the box to discover players.

It will probably also work without privileged and a more finegrained access rights control but so far nobody with more knowledge about this stood up to fix that.

We primary target on the Home Assistant add-on (as that is what most people use) and the docker image is just an additional install method but we simply are so underpowered that we do not spend a lot of time tweaking it. I hope somebody reads this and can help us fixing this properly.

Until then, I'll see if I can figure out why the pip install commands are failing on docker and not on our HA add-on.

> Here's the log with `VERBOSE` filtered out (via `grep -v " VERBOSE " music-assistant.3.log > music-assistant.3-debug.log`)
> 
> [music-assistant.3-debug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17051046/music-assistant.3-debug.log)

Thanks for that but at the same time I recommend to **disable verbose logging** (especially at global level) as it comes with some side effects. Only enable it on a PER PROVIDER base when asked specifically by one of the developers. It can cause issue son its own because the code acts a bit different when running in verbose mode (and per definition not nice to performance). So just a tip to not leave it enabled at all times or like you say, investigate the issue where the music stops. I would turn it on only on the stream controller.

That said. I think all these issues are related. So issue https://github.com/music-assistant/hass-music-assistant/issues/2893 is related to this one. If streaming fails under the hood, the queue controller has no more way to calculate where we are in the stream to show the correct song info.

If flow mode is enabled we stitch together all songs as one long stream of audio and we depend on the players accuracy of elapsed (total)time together with a calculation of how many exact bytes we processed of pcm audio per song. 

Somehow we are recently experiencing some issues with Spotify (since we had to update our librespot fork due to spotify changes to the auth api) which we're trying to tackle. Let's see if the fixes from yesterday (in b29) solve this

author: marcelveldt
body:
> I also thought of using AirPlay instead of Bluesound as the speaker provider, but I believe that even if the cover artwork, it will lower my sound quality since AirPlay is limited. 

There is nothing lowered about it. Music Assistant uses RAOP (Airplay 1) to send audio to devices, which is **LOSSLESS** CD-quality audio. So full "redbook" 44.1/16 bits.

Do not fall for all the hi-res marketing nonsense. Nobody can hear the difference between 44.1/16 and anything beyond that.
Heck. 99% of the people can not even hear the difference between a lossy compression from e.g. spotify and lossless.

So, if the metadata is important to you, I would just send the audio with Airplay and call it a day.
The metadata will then look beautiful on that M10 screen.
If you insist on playing back Hi-RES (so higher than CD quality) material, then it comes at a cost of no metadata.

@Cyanogenbot you should maybe consider also implement a "airplay mode" like the Sonos provider.
That way people can choose to use the best of 2 worlds. Use all native controls from Bluesound api, including syncing, but just send the audio stream over Airplay.

body:
@burnison thanks for your detective work on this and sorry for the slow response. We are burried in support request and only get little help on the core side of things, especially this deep down in the rabbit hole. 

What we need to figure out is if ffmpeg is the issue, librespot (who delivers the ogg stream from spotify) or a combination of those 2. Or maybe we can take spotify/librespot completely out of the picture and is the issue general to ffmpeg.

Unfortunately the issue is super hard to reproduce and reports about it are super vague where most often people dont follow up on questions or have all sorts of other issues surrounding it. From what I made up so far from the reports is that sometimes the music stops or hangs and because I added a timeout handler for a while I could indeed see it lockup but I was never able to catch it in my debugger "live" which kind of supports your conclusion this is specific to the ffmpeg build.

I'm developing on macos where I have ffmpeg 7. Not once I was able to catch this bug while I have spotted it a couple of times in user logs (after I added a Timeout guard to let the code raise on timeout).

So what we can do instead of keep looking for the needle in the haystack is maybe try switching back to Debian with ffmpeg 7. Let a few people run the beta for a week or so to see if the issue still pops up.

author: marcelveldt
body:
BTW: In your log I spot the root of all issues (which I found out today): 

```Assertion best_input >= 0 failed at fftools/ffmpeg_filter```

That is the actual bug and one that is known at ffmpeg, I traced it down into the bug tracker.

Main difference between ffmpeg 6.1 and 7 is that 6.1 then stalls and 7 aborts.
It happens because of the internal upsample that happens when the loudnorm filter is active. The loud norm filter is what we use as fallback/default volume normalization (which is dynamic) when no measurement exists.

> So, you confirm there is no way to authenticate against Spotify and/or HA when using a rev proxy without exposing MA directly?

Yes and that is also stated in our documentation. Your setup is not supported by us. You have to understand that a limited team like us can not support every advanced setup out there. We simply do not have the manpower to develop and support that.

If you run a default HAOS installation like 90% of the folks do, this will work out of the box.

>  i do not need Music Assistant to connect directly to my players as i can use HA players from Music Assistant

That is not true, the player will need to fetch the audio stream from MA. It fetches that from the MA server's stream server (by default hosted on port 8097)

One thing you could try to do is also override the base URL for the stream server, you can also do that in the settings.
But routing audio through a reverse proxy is without support from us either. Especially make sure that you do it without SSL because https adds a lot of overhead which limited microcontrollers like ESP32 in the voice PE just do not like very much.

author: marcelveldt
body:
We use PCM internally because that is how our core has been designed. From working with (floating point) PCM internally we can apply effects (like dsp but also crossfading), filters (like volume normalization) etc. on the audio without any quality loss and then we also need to be compatible with so many different player types we only decide at the end of the chain what to actually send to a player. Some player types even receive the PCM stream and then handle that in their own way but in most cases we encode to flac as this is lossless and has a nice compression ratio while being friendly for the cpu at the same time.

This is how the core is designed and it will never change, period.
The amount of cpu involved is neglectable on today's hardware. This was maybe an issue 20 years ago but not today. Other processes in MA ask way more from CPU.

So its not true that the mp3 is "converted to flac". The MA audio streaming core works with PCM. So all input audio is decoded to PCM. We want to prevent encoding again to a lossy format so that is why we use flac by default. No quality is lost at all. If a player does not support 24bits bit depth we will use dithering to bring it back to 16 bits.

All that is taken care of with the highest audio quality in mind.
Your issue has nothing to do with that conversion at all. It is because of because some buffer tresholds. We are aware of this issue and it on the radar to fix. You can simply have issues with super short audio clips, especially with chromecast as that is a bit picky where it requires at least X amount of buffer per file format. Try another player type such as slimproto and you will see it works fine. 

In any case, it has nothing to do with the internal conversion to PCM, not at all.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> but basically everything can play MP3

That is a wrong assumption

>  So why fuss with a conversion that doesn't seem to convey benefit?

Explained above. Because you want to be able to offer features such as crossfading, volume normalization, dsp etc. at high/lossless quality. Also because we have so many different output types to support.

author: marcelveldt
body:
> It's not quite equal between the two players holding the queue still, but it's working. If the player is holding the queue, does that mean it is the leader?

When using a dedicated player group (instead of manually grouping players together) the queue is held/kept on the group, which is basically a virtual player. Then a "sync leader" will be elected which will play and then the others are synced to that.

Normally a playergroup will always play to all players of the group, so they are always synced together as long as the group player is "ON".

With the option enabled for dynamic members, you can dynamically group extra members to a group or even (temporary) let members leave the group. For example when you have a "whole house" group and during the day you enable/disable players.
That will work well and without any playback of the music until you decide to ungroup the player that was the sync leader. Then the sync group needs to be reformed. The music will stop quickly for a second or 2 and automatically restart. The next player in the list will be elected as sync leader.

BTW: Electing the sync leader is just done according to order of the members list.
So when creating the group, the order in which you add the members will be deciding in how the sync leader is elected.

> The playback stutters from time to time. As I do not have these issues using DLNA I exclude network issues.

AirPlay is a rather realtime protocol with by default ALAC or PCM lossless codec. So... its by default more demanding on bandwidth that DLNA, especially if you use the MP3 codec with DLNA. So maybe you jumped into conclusions a bit too fast.

If a player is synced, any playback related commands you send will always be redirected to the sync leader (in case of manually synced/grouped players).

If all grouped are not powered and a player is not synced, if you issue a playback command, it should be handled by the player itself. Is that is still somehow handled by a group, that is a (very strange) bug.
