author: marcelveldt
body: streamserver and webserver are 2 different things. The streamserver also needs to be correct, otherwise streaming will not working for some players (most players retrieve the HTTP stream from the streamserver). In case of the streamserver its important that the players can access the port directly - although its strictly speaking another webserver, it cant be handled very well behind HTTPS/SSL due to most players have a very crappy http client so a plain HTTP session on IP (not dns name) works best.

author: marcelveldt
body:
So, the webserver takes care of the frontend and API and is normally protected behind a reverse proxy.
In case of the HA add-on (which most folks run) we do not even expose the webserver and proxy the traffic through HA ingress so we get authentication. In case you are running the MA server outside of HA, you need to take care of protecting the webserver yourself (or simply don't expose it at all).

The Streamserver takes care of serving audio to players and we also use it whenever we need unprotected redirect (e.g. for the spotify oauth callback). It should (only) be accessible from your internal network. When you start playback on e.g. a Chromecast player, the stream will be served from the streamserver (so the player receives a URL with the base url from streamserver).

body:
> However, it does take 45s between pressing play on a playlist and hearing sound. 

In that case either the hardware you run MA on is underpowered or you do not have a particular fast internet connection.
It should take about 3 till 5 seconds for Apple Music. Problem is that Apple Music (at least how it is implemented in the provider now) uses a file format which first needs to be cached fully (so all bytes received) before playback can start. This differs from other providers where we can start streaming immediately and we do not have to wait until all data is received.

Maybe @MarvinSchenkel (the maintainer of the Apple provider in MA) can give this another look someday but for now this is the best we can do. The fix introduced in 2.5.0b3 ensures that the player only starts playing when the cache is created but in your case takes a very long time.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Well, from the perspective of the receiver it actually makes sense to ignore the volume at playback start...
Imagine you're watching TV at volume 10 and then start music playback from MA but you were listening to MA music on that receiver yesterday at volume 30. Do you actually want the receiver to start the music blasting at volume 30 or at volume 10 ?

Within the Airplay protocol we have a way to send the initial volume with the call to start the music but I guess some/many manufacturers decided to ignore that for the reason I mentioned above. MA is not the only source and it is better to just keep the current volume than some randomly stored previous volume. 

Remember that only when playback is started, the player will start sending its current volume back to MA.

We could make it an option to enforce sending the volume at playback start ?

body:
Heads-up: We are updating our docs regarding the Slimproto provider. 
We will only support squeezelite based players from now on and support for any actual hardware devices is provided without guarantee or support. Plain simple reason for this is that we do not have the time or capacity to support all device specific quirks of the various squeezebox products (you already have a great product for that, its called LMS) and we're talking about 20+ years old hardware here. Even my last physical SQ hardware device now died.

We will accept PR's on the aioslimproto package and the slimproto provider to fix any compatibility issues but SB hardware devices will no longer be the focus. I will further clarify this by renaming the provider.

One idea that popped in my head is to add a LMS player provider, so people can use a intermediate LMS server in between to actually talk to the squeezebox hardware while MA will provide the media.

body:
Will have a deep dive into it as soon as I find some time, but this 'PO Token' error you are seeing does not sound like good news. A quick google reveals the following:

_Proof of Origin (PO) Token is a parameter that YouTube requires to be sent with requests from some clients. Without it, requests for the affected clients' format URLs may return HTTP Error 403, or result in your account or IP address being blocked. A PO Token is generated by an attestation provider on Web, Android and iOS platforms to attest the requests are coming from a genuine client._

To me this sounds like yet another security mechanism that Google is trying to implement to protect their content.

Problem is that its all an async operation. Send stop to a player, the player does its thing and then at some point acknowdledges the stop. Same applies for grouping commands, it happens in an async fashion.

To triple check, you could try playing a smart fade on another type of player besides snapcast.

body:
Try to avoid using HA mediaplayers whenever possible.
Owntone supports airplay and cast players, which also are natively supported by MA.

We simply have too many issues supporting the HA mediaplayers as those are not designed for actual audio playback, but more for simple automations. Often things like playback reporting is not working well leading to a flood of issues on our end.

So if possible, try to use the native MA player providers whenever possible.

We will keep this report open to look at when time allows but since there is a valid alternative, it will be lower priority.

body:
I think I found the issue. Looking at your logs, there are A LOT of 'unable to find track xxx on Apple Music' messages.

**How the built in playlists work**
The first time, it grabs all the track information from the music provider (which takes a while). After that, all the details should be saved in your database and any subsequent loads should be snappy.

However, in your case, there are A LOT of tracks in the playlist that cannot be found on Apple Music. Of course, these tracks are not cached in the local db, so it tries to find them on Apple Music every time you load the playlist.

Can you check if these tracks indeed are not available anymore on Apple Music? If so, the only solution is to clean up your playlist by removing these tracks.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Correct, welcome to Apple's confusing mess of protocols.
So, for Apple devices like Homepods and Apple TV's, we can implement other protocols like MRP to retrieve device state.

AirPlay is only a protocol to stream audio/video to a device, and receiving state updates such as volume changes is only present when we are actively streaming to a device. We cant get device state updates from an apple device while we are not actively streaming. For that we need to use the other protocols, which we will implement one day if there is enough demand

body:
Everyone, these are _very_ hard issues to replicate and solve, so you have to help me help you by providing **as many details** as possible.

- Describe the exact problem you are having: Is the time overflowing? For how long? Does it eventually go to the next song, or does it keep incrementing the time indefinitely? (etc etc)
- Which player provider are you using? These issues are almost certainly related to the player provider you are using. 
- Try the Sendspin provider by playing music on 'This device'. These are known to work as expected, so would be good to compare that in your situation.
- A video of the problem really helps ALONG with the information above.

Players integrated via the 'HA Player provider' are known to have these kind of weird issue which are unfortunately close to impossible to solve. When possible, **always** use a native player provider (eg Sonos, Airplay etc) over the HA Player provider.

In this case it means a wrong track is linked to another track, something that can actually never happen due to protection guards. A wrong track version maybe if the provider's metadata is a mess but a completely different track, not possible.

There is no such thing as an orphaned provider mapping linking to the wrong library track. Db id's are not reused.
Unless you have mapped this item yourself in the UI, this is simply not possible.

body:
In order to trace the root of this issue, we need some more information from you. Since you both deleted the cache file already, could you please:

1. Let the cache grow. Check the addon size for this
2. Install the 'Advanced SSH & Web Terminal' addon in HA
3. Open the addon, and with MA running, paste the following command in the terminal and hit ENTER

```
ADDON=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E 'addon.*music.*assistant' | head -1) && echo "Checking $ADDON..." && docker exec "$ADDON" python3 -c '
import sqlite3
import os

db_path = "/data/.cache/cache.db"
if not os.path.exists(db_path):
    db_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/music-assistant/cache.db")

# Open in read-only mode with immutable flag to avoid locking
conn = sqlite3.connect("file:" + db_path + "?mode=ro&immutable=1", uri=True)
c = conn.cursor()

print("\n=== Top Cache Categories by Size ===")
print("{:<20} {:<10} {:<10} {:<10}".format("Provider", "Category", "Records", "Size (MB)"))
print("-" * 60)
for row in c.execute("""
    SELECT provider, category, COUNT(*), ROUND(SUM(LENGTH(data))/1024.0/1024.0, 2)
    FROM cache GROUP BY provider, category 
    ORDER BY SUM(LENGTH(data)) DESC LIMIT 10
"""):
    print("{:<20} {:<10} {:<10} {:<10}".format(row[0], row[1], row[2], row[3]))

print("\n=== Overall Statistics ===")
c.execute("SELECT page_count * page_size FROM pragma_page_count(), pragma_page_size()")
file_size_bytes = c.fetchone()[0]
c.execute("SELECT SUM(LENGTH(data)) FROM cache")
data_size_bytes = c.fetchone()[0] or 0

file_size_gb = file_size_bytes / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0
data_size_gb = data_size_bytes / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0
wasted_gb = file_size_gb - data_size_gb

print("File Size:       {:.2f} GB".format(file_size_gb))
print("Actual Data:     {:.2f} GB".format(data_size_gb))
print("Wasted Space:    {:.2f} GB".format(wasted_gb))

if wasted_gb > 1.0:
    print("\nWARNING: {:.2f} GB of wasted space - VACUUM needed!".format(wasted_gb))
    
print("\nCategory Reference:")
print("  0 (player_queues) = Queue state")
print("  1 (player_queues) = Queue items (large)")
print(" 10 (music) = Search results")

conn.close()
'
``` 

This should give us a comprehensive understanding of what is taking up so much cache space.

body:
So looks like this is the issue:
```
2026-02-19 15:13:02.804 ERROR (MainThread) [music_assistant.airplay] [2026-02-19 15:13:02] [  LOG] [cliap2-linux-x8 (1077)]     main: ntpstart time too soon. Increase it by at least 3456 ms. Trying to start audio in -1 sec, 44986922 nsec
2026-02-19 15:13:02.838 WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.airplay] [2026-02-19 15:13:02] [ WARN] [cliap2-linux-x8 (1077)]     main: Unable to obtain feasible playback start time. Ignoring ntpstart argument
```

Airplay works with timestamped audio, so basically we say "here is some audio, play it at timestamp x (e.g. in 5sec from now)", but that audio seems to reach your player too late, i.e. that timestamp is already in the past. 

Questions:
* Does playing audio from your phone instantly start playback, or does playing it to both delay the audio start to the slowest time (e.g. your soundcore player)
* I see you are using Airplay 2. Have you tried this with Airplay 1 / RAOP? Please give this a go and also include verbose logs from when you play with Airplay 1

This is more and more starting to sound like a Sonos speaker issue where they might have broken mDNS discovery. HA, MA Sonos S1 (and probably Sonos app itself) all use the (ancient) SSDP protocol to discover speakers. The Sonos (S2) provider exclusively uses mDNS, so maybe those speakers have issues with that since the latest update? 

Have you tried restarting the speaker (like take it out of the outlet, wait a few minutes and re-apply power). That sometimes helps with these kind of quirks. Another thing to try is factory resetting this specific speaker and re-adding it to your Sonos home.

body:
I was looking at your logs and thinking about maybe we should be a bit more forgiving with the ping timeout or only mark the player as 'unavailable' after 2 consecutive failed pings. However, the logs clearly mention:
_"Player Basement Sonos disconnected prematurely from stream for Iron Maiden - Where Eagles Dare (2015 Remaster)"_ before we mark it as unavailable, indicating that the player stopped consuming from the MA stream.

Few questions:
- What Sonos speakers are we talking about here? Play:1s?
- Do you have those speakers integrated in HA via the Sonos integration? If so, please try disabling that and see if that improves the situation
 
Especially older (ie slower) Sonos hardware will respond heavily to multiple clients (HA _and_ MA) spamming the upnp api. This could freeze them, causing the player to lockup and stop streaming from MA. This is also why we are not instantly resubscribing during the cooldown, to avoid hammering those poor devices.

Well.. What group do you want to create here? The reason is very simple: There are no candidates that can be grouped.

- You only have two devices, a squeezelite device and a sendspin device
- Those two devices cannot be natively synced (two different protocols)

Those groups will only show candidates that can be *natively* grouped together to play in perfect sync.

If you want to group the squeezelite device and the web browser in your video you need to use a Universal Group, but be aware that they won't be in perfect sync.

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
I have some bad news unfortunately :(. 

TLDR: This speaker (and other newer Chromecast speakers) will not work with Sendspin

Longer read: To make Sendspin work with Chromecast based devices, we rely on the (bloated) implementation of the Cast protocol, which is browser based. We basically run a browser version of Sendspin inside the on-device browser of the Chromecast device. Newer devices implement the 'Google Cast for Audio (GC4A) 2.0', which is a lightweight (read non bloated) implementation that simply just does not implement the required audio API's we require to run Sendspin.

The 'good' news is that we are able to detect this so a future version of MA will automatically disable the bridge if it finds it to be incompatible.

Quote from the Cast docs:
```
Available GC4A 2.0 Devices

This is a non-comprehensive list of GC4A 2.0 devices:

Bose: Wifi Speaker and Smart Soundbars
JBL: Charge 5 Wi-Fi / Boombox 3 Wi-Fi / Authentics 200, 300, and 500
Samsung: Music Frame / Soundbars
LG: Soundbars S90TY/SG10TY/SE70Q/S80Q/S90Q
Bang & Olufsen Beosound 2 / Beocore Connect
Sonoro Maestro 2 / Meisterstruck 2
Cambridge Audio MXN10
KEF LS60 / LSX II
Teufel Motiv Home
Nordic Argon Audio
WiiM CI MOD S / Ultra
```

@OzGav can we add this to our docs?

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
No Sendspin is not a Chromecast wrapper. We just found a way to host a Sendspin **client** on Chromecast **devices** by running it in the browser on the Chromecast device.

Sendspin needs **timestamped audio** (ie play this audio at this exact time) for synchronisation. The only other protocol that supports this is Airplay, which means we can only bridge Sendspin to Airplay and not other protocols such as DLNA and Squeezelite which are basically 'fire-and-forget' protocols that say 'play this url from the server'.

It is still not clear. Tell me exactly what your issue is. Don't refer to existing issues. Don't make your own wrong assumptions and weird AI analysis. That does not help and causes confusion. Keep it to the point of describing your issue.

It is fine (and even encouraged) to tell what worked before, what you already tested yourself.

Official certified AirPlay devices do not need any latency correction at all. They are perfectly aligned per factory default.
You would only need a latency correction (at AirPlay level) for 3rd party AirPlay implementations. body:
So your Denon is a bit of a weird outlier. It basically does this:
1. Sends 'preventplayback=1'. Devices usually send this when the device has switched input for example, so MA knows to stop streaming which is what we do when we receive such a command
2. A few milliseconds later the denon sends 'preventplayback=0', meaning "I am ready to receive playback"

I implemented a fix so that MA basically ignores the first message when the second arrives quickly after ;-)

body:
> I'm now running 2.9.0b11 and have re-enabled smart fades analysis. I manually triggered the background scan (at 18:56 on 12 May) and CPU was no higher than 17% for the 4 hours and MA performance appeared unaffected (finishing at 22:56 on 12 May). It scanned 48 files, but seemed to pick some large podcast files which individually timed out after 300s each. The task then ran automatically at midnight as expected and scanned the same 48 files - it did not start from where it previously finished, so I assume it will keep scanning the same files every time it runs. See attached log.
> 
> [music-assistant.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27696590/music-assistant.log)

That's because they are defined as `Tracks` and not as `Podcasts` in your MA instance. We automatically skip for example a Smart fades analysis for non-Tracks, but if you tell MA that `13 Minutes To The Moon - s2 e01 - Time Bomb Apollo13.mp3` is a track, then we have no way of knowing it's a Podcast.

You should create a separate instance for your filesystem provider and correctly set the config value for `Content type in media folder(s)`

body:
Like I said before, you can still use the standard crossfade, which is available for all systems/cpu's.
Smartfades in 2.8 was more or less an enhanced crossfade. In 2.9 it has actually become smart(er) thanks to the special analyzing of the audio. 

We could consider adding a "override the requirements, run this beast purely in software" but if your system is not beefy enough it will most likely take it down. I can have a look if we can offer such option but the current hard check is there for a reason: during beta we had some folks taking down their system as they were running MA on a potato.

Maybe previously you were also using standard crossfade ?

author: marcelveldt
body:
I can add the option, but it will be at your own risk. These older CPU's are simply not optimized for these calculations so it will be very inefficient. Same applies to a lot of things nowadays. Even something simple as a json encoder/decoder heavily benefits from AVX2. At the same time I understand the wish to keep using older hardware as long as possible so that is why I'll give it a try but expect that you will keep running into more of these issues as software evolves. 

I spent some time today tweaking the code and at least we now have a core budget cap so worst what can happen is that we peg half of the cores and that together with some throttling might actually make it work reasonable. I'm still going to put it behind a scary flag because I'm worried of people breaking their setups trying to enable all these powerful features on some potato hardware.

author: marcelveldt
body:
Looked into it (and tested it). It wont be possible, I'm sorry. It will be so slow that your CPU is going to run circles around its own tail and worst of all, playback will be affected. That is too much of a risk. We will basically offer an option for you to kill your machine, let's not go there :-). Let alone the added maintenance burden for us on the project (and possible failure points added).

AVX2 is available in x86 CPU's since 2013 so that is already 13 years ago.
Even a descent ARM64 cpu nowadays (like on a pi4/5) has more optimizations than those very old cpu's.
On top of that most people seem to be running on old Celeron CPU's so its tradeoff on top of tradeoff.
A rare situation of a heavy i5/i7 or even Xeon _might_ actually be able to run it but that is so rare that it's not worth the tradeoff for us in the project. Hope you all understand this.

BTW:
Reason why it worked in MA 2.8 is that smartfades then was not as smart as it is now. The current standard crossfade is more like the 2.8 smartfades. The new smartfades is more like a dj that can analyse the music and make decisions on that. Its exactly this analysis which requires these newer CPU instructions (which is already great since we don't need to rely on a GPU or AI accelerator, which puts the bar even higher to offer such advanced features in an opensource project).

So if you run into this today;
- Ensure you have a AVX2 capable CPU on x86 (or use a ARM64 cpu)
- If you run virtualized and you know your cpu supports AVX2, ensure that your VM gets passed the host cpu
- Ensure you have AT LEAST 4GB of RAM and 2 CPU cores

If your setup does not have any of these requirements, you won't be able to add/enable the smartfades/sonic analysis.
If it's already added on your setup (due to the missing check in 2.9.0) and you se ethe "provider setup failed" error, simply delete the provider from the config.

Standard crossfade is available on all setups.

@LaneaLucy sorry I mis interpreted your previous reply. I had a look at this and I think this is because of the internal buffer settings of the snapcast server. I added an advanced setting for this for now. If this works, we will look into a way to automatically set it.

Could you please test this with the DEV App? This won't interfere with your existing installation of MA, as it is a completely isolated installation of MA.

- In Home Assistant, make sure that 'Advanced mode' is 'ON' in your profile settings
- Go to 'Settings > Apps' and stop your current MA App
- Click 'Install an app' and install the 'Music Assistant DEV SERVER'
- Go to the configuration tab of the App
- Type `fix/4377-snapcast-announcement-buffer` for server_repo
- Type `main` for frontend_repo
- Start the app. This will take longer than you are used to

Then to test the new setting:
**Check your Snapcast server's buffer:**
- Open `/etc/snapserver.conf` on the machine running snapserver
- Look for `buffer = ...` under the `[stream]` section (if it's absent or commented out, the default is `1000` ms)
- If you start snapserver with command-line args instead, check for `--stream.buffer=...`

**Set it in Music Assistant:**
- Go to **Settings → Providers → Snapcast**, and enable "show advanced settings"
- Set **"Snapserver buffer size"** to the same value in ms
- Save — the provider reloads automatically, then test an announcement

We have a fix available, could you please test this with the DEV App? This won't interfere with your existing installation of MA, as it is a completely isolated installation of MA.

- In Home Assistant, make sure that 'Advanced mode' is 'ON' in your profile settings
- Go to 'Settings > Apps' and stop your current MA App
- Click 'Install an app' and install the 'Music Assistant DEV SERVER'
- Go to the configuration tab of the App
- Type `pr-4683` for server_repo
- Type `main` for frontend_repo
- Start the app. This will take longer than you are used to
- Test if the issue has been resolved

body:
You should still be able to run this yourself though:

```
mkdir -p ./mass-dev
cat > ./mass-dev/options.json <<'EOF'
{
  "log_level": "debug",
  "server_repo": "pr-4685",
  "frontend_repo": "main",
  "safe_mode": false
}
EOF

docker run -d --name mass-dev \
  --network host \
  -v "$(pwd)/mass-dev:/data" \
  ghcr.io/music-assistant/music_assistant_dev:latest
```

Our dev addon is jhttps://github.com/music-assistant/home-assistant-addon/tree/main/music_assistant_dev :).

author: MarvinSchenkel
body:
We will never be able to update the `media_position` in HA at every second, because this puts too much pressure on HA. So the trick is that we both update
- `media_position`
- `media_position_updated_at`

Then when you open the media entity in HA, the elapsed time in the widget should match the MA time because HA will just keep extrapolating the elapsed time based on the two properties above.

Can you confirm that the progress bar you see when you click the media entity is in sync with MA?
